class TarlVerdict(enum.StrEnum): 
18class TarlVerdict(StrEnum):
19    DENY = "DENY"
20    ESCALATE = "ESCALATE"
21    ALLOW = "ALLOW"
22
23    def __str__(self) -> str:
24        return self.value
25
26    def __lt__(self, other: object) -> bool:
27        if not isinstance(other, TarlVerdict):
28            return NotImplemented
29        return _VERDICT_RANK[self] < _VERDICT_RANK[other]
30
31    def __le__(self, other: object) -> bool:
32        if not isinstance(other, TarlVerdict):
33            return NotImplemented
34        return _VERDICT_RANK[self] <= _VERDICT_RANK[other]
35
36    def __gt__(self, other: object) -> bool:
37        if not isinstance(other, TarlVerdict):
38            return NotImplemented
39        return _VERDICT_RANK[self] > _VERDICT_RANK[other]
40
41    def __ge__(self, other: object) -> bool:
42        if not isinstance(other, TarlVerdict):
43            return NotImplemented
44        return _VERDICT_RANK[self] >= _VERDICT_RANK[other]
45
46    @staticmethod
47    def meet(a: TarlVerdict, b: TarlVerdict) -> TarlVerdict:
48        """Restrictive composition (∧): min in safety ordering."""
49        return a if _VERDICT_RANK[a] <= _VERDICT_RANK[b] else b
50
51    @staticmethod
52    def join(a: TarlVerdict, b: TarlVerdict) -> TarlVerdict:  # type: ignore[override]
53        """Permissive composition (∨): max in safety ordering.
54
55        Intentionally shadows ``str.join`` (this enum subclasses ``str``); it is
56        the lattice join over verdicts, not string concatenation.
57        """
58        return a if _VERDICT_RANK[a] >= _VERDICT_RANK[b] else b

@dataclass
class TarlDecision: 
174@dataclass
175class TarlDecision:
176    """Result of evaluating a T.A.R.L. policy against a context."""
177    verdict: TarlVerdict
178    reason: str = ""
179    rule_index: int = -1
180    matched_rule: str | None = None
181    expires_at: str | None = None    # ISO-8601 UTC; set for time-bound verdicts
182
183    def __str__(self) -> str:
184        s = f"[{self.verdict.value}] {self.reason}"
185        if self.expires_at:
186            s += f" (expires: {self.expires_at})"
187        return s
188
189    def is_expired(self) -> bool:
190        """
191        Return True if this decision carried a time-bound verdict that has
192        now elapsed.  Always False when expires_at is not set.
193
194        The engine stamps expires_at at evaluation time but never
195        re-evaluates automatically.  Callers that cache decisions must call
196        this method before acting on a stored result and re-evaluate when it
197        returns True.
198        """
199        if self.expires_at is None:
200            return False
201        import datetime
202        try:
203            exp = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(
204                self.expires_at.replace("Z", "+00:00")
205            )
206            if exp.tzinfo is None or exp.utcoffset() is None:
207                return True
208            return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC) >= exp
209        except (AttributeError, TypeError, ValueError):
210            return True

@dataclass
class TarlPolicy: 
117@dataclass
118class TarlPolicy:
119    """Ordered decision function: P = [r₁, r₂, ..., rₙ] over context space."""
120    rules: list[TarlRule] = field(default_factory=list)
121    source: str = ""
122    name: str = "unnamed"
123    # Phase 2: composition
124    parent: str | None = None
125    composition: CompositionOp | None = None
126    includes: list[TarlPolicyRef] = field(default_factory=list)
127    has_stop: bool = False
128    # Phase 5: temporal governance
129    version: str | None = None
130    supersedes: str | None = None
131    valid_from: str | None = None      # ISO-8601; policy not effective before this
132    valid_until: str | None = None     # ISO-8601; policy expires after this
133    on_expiry: TarlVerdict | None = None  # verdict when outside window (default ESCALATE)
134    if_unresolved_after: int | None = None  # seconds; auto-expire from valid_from
135    revert_to: str | None = None            # policy name to evaluate on succession
136
137    def __str__(self) -> str:
138        header = f"policy {self.name}"
139        if self.composition and self.parent:
140            header += f" {self.composition.value} {self.parent}"
141        if self.version:
142            header += f" v{self.version}"
143        lines = [f"{header}:"]
144        if self.valid_from:
145            lines.append(f"  valid_from: {self.valid_from}")
146        if self.valid_until:
147            lines.append(f"  valid_until: {self.valid_until}")
148        if self.supersedes:
149            lines.append(f"  supersedes: {self.supersedes}")
150        if self.on_expiry:
151            lines.append(f"  on_expiry: {self.on_expiry.value}")
152        if self.if_unresolved_after is not None and self.revert_to:
153            ds = self.if_unresolved_after
154            if ds % 3600 == 0:
155                dur = f"{ds // 3600}h"
156            elif ds % 60 == 0:
157                dur = f"{ds // 60}m"
158            else:
159                dur = f"{ds}s"
160            lines.append(f"  if_unresolved_after: {dur} => revert_to: {self.revert_to}")
161        for ref in self.includes:
162            alias_part = f" AS {ref.alias}" if ref.alias else ""
163            if ref.is_file:
164                lines.append(f'  INCLUDE "{ref.name}"{alias_part}')
165            else:
166                lines.append(f"  INCLUDE {ref.name}{alias_part}")
167        for r in self.rules:
168            lines.append(f"  {r}")
169        if self.has_stop:
170            lines.append("  STOP")
171        return "\n".join(lines)

Ordered decision function: P = [r₁, r₂, ..., rₙ] over context space.

113                s += f" for: {ds}s"
114        return s

@dataclass
class TarlPolicySet: 
213@dataclass
214class TarlPolicySet:
215    """
216    A named composition of multiple policies evaluated with set operators.
217
218    groups: list of (SetOp, [policy_name, ...])
219    Each group produces a verdict via its operator.
220    The final verdict is the meet (∧) of all group verdicts.
221    """
222    name: str
223    groups: list[tuple[SetOp, list[str]]] = field(default_factory=list)
224    default_verdict: TarlVerdict = TarlVerdict.DENY
225    source: str = ""
226
227    def __str__(self) -> str:
228        lines = [f"policy_set {self.name}:"]
229        for op, names in self.groups:
230            lines.append(f"  combine {op.value} [{', '.join(names)}]")
231        lines.append(f"  default: {self.default_verdict.value}")
232        return "\n".join(lines)

@dataclass
class TarlProof: 
235@dataclass
236class TarlProof:
237    """
238    Integrity certificate of a policy evaluation.
239
240    Π = (H(P), H(original-c), H(canonical-c), R, N, C, H(S), S,
241         k, v, t_exp, T, σ)
242      H(P) — SHA-256 of exact policy source used
243      H(original-c) — SHA-256 of the caller-supplied context snapshot
244      H(canonical-c) — SHA-256 of the exact representation evaluated
245      R    — authoritative context representation identifier
246      N    — transformation/normalization algorithm identifier and version
247      C    — representation collision/conflict status
248      H(S) — SHA-256 fingerprint of the explicit context schema
249      S    — schema representation identifier and validation status
250      k    — matched rule index (-1 = DEFAULT_DENY)
251      v    — final verdict
252      t_exp — optional expiry of a time-bound matched-rule verdict
253      T    — evaluation trace: [{rule_index, condition, matched}, ...]
254      σ    — optional HMAC-SHA256 tag or Ed25519 signature over the canonical
255             encoding
256
257    Runtime-generated proofs can be unsigned when no signing key is configured,
258    but the verifier rejects unsigned proofs by default. HMAC-SHA256 remains
259    available as a symmetric compatibility mode: it is forgeable by any party
260    that holds the key, including a verifier. Use Ed25519 for non-repudiable
261    asymmetric proof signatures where the verifier has only the public key.
262    """
263    policy_hash: str          # "sha256:<hex>"
264    context_hash: str         # "sha256:<hex>"
265    rule_index: int           # -1 = DEFAULT_DENY
266    matched_condition: str    # "" for DEFAULT_DENY
267    verdict: TarlVerdict
268    evaluated_at: str         # ISO-8601 UTC
269    trace: list[dict]         # [{rule_index, condition, matched}, ...]
270    signature: str            # "hmac-sha256:<hex>", "ed25519:<hex>", or ""
271    key_id: str               # signing key identifier or ""
272    original_context_hash: str | None = None
273    canonical_context_hash: str | None = None
274    context_representation_id: str | None = None
275    normalization_algorithm_id: str | None = None
276    normalization_version: str | None = None
277    context_conflict_status: str | None = None
278    context_schema_hash: str | None = None
279    context_schema_representation_id: str | None = None
280    context_schema_validation_status: str | None = None
281    expires_at: str | None = None
282
283    def _context_binding(self) -> dict[str, str | None]:
284        return {
285            "original_context_hash": self.original_context_hash,
286            "canonical_context_hash": self.canonical_context_hash,
287            "context_representation_id": self.context_representation_id,
288            "normalization_algorithm_id": self.normalization_algorithm_id,
289            "normalization_version": self.normalization_version,
290            "context_conflict_status": self.context_conflict_status,
291        }
292
293    def _schema_binding(self) -> dict[str, str | None]:
294        return {
295            "context_schema_hash": self.context_schema_hash,
296            "context_schema_representation_id": (
297                self.context_schema_representation_id
298            ),
299            "context_schema_validation_status": (
300                self.context_schema_validation_status
301            ),
302        }
303
304    def canonical_bytes(self) -> bytes:
305        """Deterministic serialisation used for signing and verification."""
306        import json
307        data = {
308            "policy_hash": self.policy_hash,
309            "context_hash": self.context_hash,
310            "rule_index": self.rule_index,
311            "matched_condition": self.matched_condition,
312            "verdict": self.verdict.value,
313            "evaluated_at": self.evaluated_at,
314            "trace": self.trace,
315        }
316        if self.expires_at is not None:
317            data["expires_at"] = self.expires_at
318        binding = self._context_binding()
319        if any(value is not None for value in binding.values()):
320            data["context_binding"] = binding
321        schema_binding = self._schema_binding()
322        if any(value is not None for value in schema_binding.values()):
323            data["context_schema_binding"] = schema_binding
324        return json.dumps(
325            data, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False
326        ).encode('utf-8')
327
328    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
329        data = {
330            "policy_hash": self.policy_hash,
331            "context_hash": self.context_hash,
332            "rule_index": self.rule_index,
333            "matched_condition": self.matched_condition,
334            "verdict": self.verdict.value,
335            "evaluated_at": self.evaluated_at,
336            "expires_at": self.expires_at,
337            "trace": list(self.trace),
338            "signature": self.signature,
339            "key_id": self.key_id,
340        }
341        data.update(self._context_binding())
342        data.update(self._schema_binding())
343        return data
344
345    def to_json(self) -> str:
346        import json
347        return json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=2, allow_nan=False)
348
349    @classmethod
350    def from_dict(cls, d: dict) -> TarlProof:
351        return cls(
352            policy_hash=d["policy_hash"],
353            context_hash=d["context_hash"],
354            rule_index=d["rule_index"],
355            matched_condition=d.get("matched_condition", ""),
356            verdict=TarlVerdict(d["verdict"]),
357            evaluated_at=d["evaluated_at"],
358            trace=d.get("trace", []),
359            signature=d.get("signature", ""),
360            key_id=d.get("key_id", ""),
361            original_context_hash=d.get("original_context_hash"),
362            canonical_context_hash=d.get("canonical_context_hash"),
363            context_representation_id=d.get("context_representation_id"),
364            normalization_algorithm_id=d.get("normalization_algorithm_id"),
365            normalization_version=d.get("normalization_version"),
366            context_conflict_status=d.get("context_conflict_status"),
367            context_schema_hash=d.get("context_schema_hash"),
368            context_schema_representation_id=d.get(
369                "context_schema_representation_id"
370            ),
371            context_schema_validation_status=d.get(

373            ),

375        )

Integrity certificate of a policy evaluation.

Π = (H(P), H(original-c), H(canonical-c), R, N, C, H(S), S, k, v, t_exp, T, σ) H(P) — SHA-256 of exact policy source used H(original-c) — SHA-256 of the caller-supplied context snapshot H(canonical-c) — SHA-256 of the exact representation evaluated R — authoritative context representation identifier N — transformation/normalization algorithm identifier and version C — representation collision/conflict status H(S) — SHA-256 fingerprint of the explicit context schema S — schema representation identifier and validation status k — matched rule index (-1 = DEFAULT_DENY) v — final verdict t_exp — optional expiry of a time-bound matched-rule verdict T — evaluation trace: [{rule_index, condition, matched}, ...] σ — optional HMAC-SHA256 tag or Ed25519 signature over the canonical encoding

Runtime-generated proofs can be unsigned when no signing key is configured, but the verifier rejects unsigned proofs by default. HMAC-SHA256 remains available as a symmetric compatibility mode: it is forgeable by any party that holds the key, including a verifier. Use Ed25519 for non-repudiable asymmetric proof signatures where the verifier has only the public key.

308            "policy_hash": self.policy_hash,

322        if any(value is not None for value in schema_binding.values()):
323            data["context_schema_binding"] = schema_binding
324        return json.dumps(
325            data, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False
326        ).encode('utf-8')

class TarlRuntime: 
 99class TarlRuntime:
100    """
101    TARL policy runtime:
102    - LRU decision cache (128 entries)
103    - ThreadPoolExecutor for parallel rule evaluation
104    - Adaptive ordering (most-frequently-matched rules evaluated first)
105    - Dynamic source registry for source:name condition references
106    """
107
108    def __init__(
109        self,
110        policy: TarlPolicy | None = None,
111        max_workers: int = 4,
112    ):
113        self.policy = policy or TarlPolicy()
114        self.cache = LRUCache(maxsize=128)
115        self.executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers)
116        self._hit_counts: dict = {}
117        self._throw_counts: dict = {}   # rule_index -> number of evaluation exceptions
118        self._sources: dict = {}
119        self._signing_keys: dict = {}   # key_id -> bytes (HMAC secrets)
120        self._ed25519_signing_keys: dict = {}  # key_id -> Ed25519PrivateKey
121        self._signing_key_id: str = ""  # active key
122        self._signing_alg: str = ""     # "hmac-sha256" or "ed25519"
123        self._archive = None            # TarlAuditArchive | None
124        self._context_schema: ContextSchema | None = None
125        self._context_schema_origin = "none"
126        self._require_audit = False     # fail closed if audit cannot persist
127        # Trusted time source for temporal checks; None => host clock.
128        self._clock: Callable[[], datetime.datetime | None] | None = None
129
130    def set_clock(self, clock) -> "TarlRuntime":
131        """Use a trusted time source for temporal-policy checks instead of the
132        host clock. ``clock`` is a zero-arg callable returning a timezone-aware
133        ``datetime`` (typically obtained by verifying a signed-time assertion via
134        ``utf.tarl.clock.TrustedClock``). A spoofed system clock then cannot
135        satisfy a temporal window (C043). Returns self."""
136        if not callable(clock):
137            raise TypeError("clock must be callable")
138        self._clock = clock
139        return self
140
141    def _now(self) -> datetime.datetime | None:
142        if self._clock is None:
143            return None
144        try:
145            current = self._clock()
146        except Exception as exc:
147            raise ContextResolutionError(
148                f"trusted clock failure: {exc}",
149                state=ContextResolutionState.TYPE_ERROR,
150            ) from exc
151        if not isinstance(current, datetime.datetime):
152            raise ContextResolutionError(
153                "trusted clock failure: expected a datetime value",
154                state=ContextResolutionState.TYPE_ERROR,
155            )
156        if current.tzinfo is None or current.utcoffset() is None:
157            raise ContextResolutionError(
158                "trusted clock failure: datetime must be timezone-aware",
159                state=ContextResolutionState.TYPE_ERROR,
160            )
161        return current.astimezone(datetime.UTC)
162
163    def set_require_audit(self, required: bool = True) -> "TarlRuntime":
164        """When True and an audit archive is attached, a failure to persist a
165        proof downgrades the decision to a fail-closed DENY (C038): execution
166        cannot proceed if the required audit record could not be written."""
167        self._require_audit = required
168        return self
169
170    def _persist(
171        self,
172        policy: TarlPolicy,
173        ctx: PreparedContext,
174        decision: TarlDecision,
175        proof: TarlProof,
176    ) -> tuple[TarlDecision, TarlProof]:
177        """Store the proof; on a persistence failure, fail closed when audit is
178        required. Returns the (possibly downgraded) ``(decision, proof)``."""
179        if self._archive is None:
180            return decision, proof
181        try:
182            self._archive.store(proof, expires_at=decision.expires_at)
183            return decision, proof
184        except Exception as exc:  # disk full, DoS on the audit sink, etc.
185            if not self._require_audit:
186                return decision, proof
187            denied = TarlDecision(
188                verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
189                reason=f"fail-closed: required audit could not be persisted: {exc}",
190            )
191            denied_proof = self._generate_proof(
192                policy, ctx, denied, -1,
193                [{"kind": "audit-fail", "matched": False, "reason": str(exc)}],
194                schema_binding={
195                    "hash": proof.context_schema_hash or "",
196                    "representation_id": (
197                        proof.context_schema_representation_id or ""
198                    ),
199                    "status": (
200                        proof.context_schema_validation_status
201                        or "not_evaluated"
202                    ),
203                },
204                evaluation_time=datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(
205                    proof.evaluated_at.replace("Z", "+00:00")
206                ),
207            )
208            return denied, denied_proof
209
210    # ── Context schema ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
211
212    def set_context_schema(self, schema: ContextSchema) -> "TarlRuntime":
213        """Attach a ``utf.tarl.schema.ContextSchema``. When set, every context is
214        validated before any rule runs; a missing required field or a
215        type-confused value short-circuits to the schema's fail-closed verdict
216        (DENY by default) instead of silently matching a permissive later rule.
217        Returns self for chaining."""
218        if type(schema) is not ContextSchema:
219            raise TypeError("context schema must be a ContextSchema")
220        # Validate and fingerprint at registration time so malformed schema
221        # configuration cannot reach an authorization path.
222        schema.fingerprint()
223        self._context_schema = schema
224        self._context_schema_origin = "explicit"
225        return self
226
227    def ensure_context_schema(self) -> bool:
228        """Attach a complete derived schema when authority use needs one.
229
230        Plain evaluation remains available without a schema, but load-bearing
231        consumers call this method before relying on ALLOW.  Incomplete or
232        ambiguous derivation leaves the runtime unbound so the consumer's
233        positive-proof admissibility gate fails closed.
234        """
235        if self._context_schema is not None:
236            return True
237        try:
238            from utf.thirsty_lang.proof_obligations import derive_context_schema
239
240            derived = derive_context_schema(self.policy.source)
241            if not derived.complete:
242                return False
243            self.set_context_schema(ContextSchema.from_dict(derived.to_dict()))
244            self._context_schema_origin = "derived"
245        except Exception:
246            return False
247        return True
248
249    def _schema_for_evaluation(
250        self,
251        policy: TarlPolicy,
252        *,
253        policy_override: bool,
254    ) -> tuple[ContextSchema | None, str]:
255        """Resolve the schema that belongs to the policy being evaluated.
256
257        A schema derived for ``self.policy`` must never be reused for a
258        different ``policy_text`` override. Explicit schemas are caller-bound
259        and remain applicable; derived schemas are regenerated per override.
260        """
261        if not policy_override or self._context_schema_origin != "derived":
262            return self._context_schema, ""
263        try:
264            from utf.thirsty_lang.proof_obligations import derive_context_schema
265
266            derived = derive_context_schema(policy.source)
267            if not derived.complete:
268                return None, (
269                    "context schema could not be derived completely for the "
270                    "evaluated policy override"
271                )
272            return ContextSchema.from_dict(derived.to_dict()), ""
273        except Exception as exc:
274            return None, (
275                "context schema could not be derived for the evaluated "
276                f"policy override: {exc}"
277            )
278
279    @staticmethod
280    def _binding_for_schema(
281        schema: ContextSchema | None,
282        status: str,
283    ) -> dict[str, str]:
284        """Return proof metadata for one exact context schema."""
285        if schema is None:
286            return {
287                "hash": "",
288                "representation_id": "",
289                "status": "error" if status == "error" else "not_configured",
290            }
291        try:
292            schema_hash = schema.fingerprint()
293            representation_id = schema.representation_id
294        except Exception:
295            return {
296                "hash": "",
297                "representation_id": "",
298                "status": "error",
299            }
300        return {
301            "hash": schema_hash,
302            "representation_id": representation_id,
303            "status": status,
304        }
305
306    def _schema_binding(self, status: str) -> dict[str, str]:
307        """Return proof metadata for the runtime's configured schema."""
308        return self._binding_for_schema(self._context_schema, status)
309
310    def _validate_context_schema(
311        self,
312        context: PreparedContext,
313        schema: ContextSchema | None,
314    ) -> tuple["TarlDecision | None", dict[str, str]]:
315        """Validate once and return both decision and proof-bound result."""
316        if schema is None:
317            return None, self._binding_for_schema(None, "not_configured")
318
319        before_binding = self._binding_for_schema(schema, "not_evaluated")
320        if before_binding["status"] == "error":
321            return (
322                TarlDecision(
323                    verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
324                    reason="context schema configuration is invalid",
325                ),
326                before_binding,
327            )
328        schema_violation_verdict = schema.on_violation
329
330        try:
331            violations = ContextSchema.validate(schema, context)
332            context_unchanged = (
333                hash_context(context.canonical) == context.canonical_context_hash
334            )
335            after_binding = self._binding_for_schema(schema, "passed")
336        except Exception as exc:
337            binding = self._binding_for_schema(schema, "error")
338            binding["status"] = "error"
339            return (
340                TarlDecision(
341                    verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
342                    reason=f"context schema validation failed: {exc}",
343                ),
344                binding,
345            )
346
347        if (
348            not context_unchanged
349            or after_binding["hash"] != before_binding["hash"]
350            or after_binding["representation_id"]
351            != before_binding["representation_id"]
352        ):
353            after_binding["status"] = "error"
354            return (
355                TarlDecision(
356                    verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
357                    reason=(
358                        "context schema validation mutated its schema or "
359                        "evaluation context"
360                    ),
361                ),
362                after_binding,
363            )
364
365        if not violations:
366            return None, after_binding
367
368        after_binding["status"] = "failed"
369        return (
370            TarlDecision(
371                verdict=schema_violation_verdict,
372                reason="context schema violation: " + "; ".join(violations),
373            ),
374            after_binding,
375        )
376
377    def _schema_decision(
378        self,
379        context: PreparedContext,
380        schema: ContextSchema | None,
381    ) -> "TarlDecision | None":
382        """Return a fail-closed decision when ``context`` violates the schema,
383        else None."""
384        decision, _binding = self._validate_context_schema(context, schema)
385        return decision
386
387    # ── Audit archive ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
388
389    def set_archive(self, archive) -> "TarlRuntime":
390        """
391        Attach a TarlAuditArchive.  Proofs generated by evaluate_with_proof()
392        are stored automatically.  Returns self for chaining.
393        """
394        self._archive = archive
395        return self
396
397    # ── Signing key registry ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
398
399    def set_signing_key(
400        self, key_id: str, secret: bytes
401    ) -> "TarlRuntime":
402        """
403        Register an HMAC-SHA256 signing key for proof generation.
404        The most recently set key becomes the active key.
405        Returns self for chaining.
406        """
407        self._signing_keys[key_id] = secret
408        self._signing_key_id = key_id
409        self._signing_alg = "hmac-sha256"
410        return self
411
412    def set_ed25519_signing_key(
413        self, key_id: str, private_key: bytes | Ed25519PrivateKey
414    ) -> "TarlRuntime":
415        """
416        Register an Ed25519 private key for proof generation.
417
418        ``private_key`` may be a cryptography Ed25519PrivateKey or the raw
419        32-byte private seed accepted by Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes().
420        The most recently set key becomes the active key.
421        """
422        if isinstance(private_key, Ed25519PrivateKey):
423            key = private_key
424        else:
425            key = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(private_key)
426        self._ed25519_signing_keys[key_id] = key
427        self._signing_key_id = key_id
428        self._signing_alg = "ed25519"
429        return self
430
431    # ── Source registry ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
432
433    def register_source(
434        self, name: str, provider
435    ) -> "TarlRuntime":
436        """
437        Bind a data provider to source:<name> condition references.
438
439        provider — a strict JSON value (commonly a list) or a zero-arg
440                   callable that returns one each time it is called.
441        Returns self for chaining.
442        """
443        if (
444            type(name) is not str
445            or not name
446            or not all(char.isalnum() or char == "_" for char in name)
447        ):
448            raise ValueError(
449                "registered source name must be non-empty and contain only "
450                "letters, numbers, or underscores"
451            )
452        self._sources[name] = provider
453        return self
454
455    def _inject_sources(self, context: dict) -> dict:
456        """Resolve all registered sources and inject into a context copy."""
457        if not self._sources:
458            return dict(context)
459        source_context = {}
460        for name, provider in self._sources.items():
461            try:
462                value = provider() if callable(provider) else provider
463            except Exception as exc:
464                raise ContextResolutionError(
465                    f"registered source '{name}' could not be resolved: {exc}",
466                    state=ContextResolutionState.MISSING,
467                    path=f"source:{name}",
468                ) from exc
469            source_context[f"source:{name}"] = value
470        return compose_context_layers(
471            ("caller context", context),
472            ("registered sources", source_context),
473        )
474
475    def _prepare_evaluation_context(self, context: dict) -> PreparedContext:
476        """Freeze caller input, inject sources, then freeze the evaluated state."""
477        original = prepare_context(context)
478        enriched = self._inject_sources(original.canonical)
479        evaluated = prepare_context(enriched, allow_source_keys=True)
480        algorithm = (
481            "identity"
482            if original.original_context_hash == evaluated.canonical_context_hash
483            else "tarl.registered-source-injection"
484        )
485        return PreparedContext(
486            canonical=evaluated.canonical,
487            original_context_hash=original.original_context_hash,
488            canonical_context_hash=evaluated.canonical_context_hash,
489            normalization_algorithm_id=algorithm,
490        )
491
492    # ── Policy management ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
493
494    def throw_stats(self) -> dict:
495        """
496        Return throw counts per rule index.
497
498        **What the number means:**
499        Counts reflect distinct contexts that missed the cache and threw, not
500        total call frequency.  A rule that throws on one bad context evaluated
501        a thousand times shows throw_count == 1, not 1000, because cached
502        results bypass rule evaluation entirely.  The stat answers "how many
503        distinct inputs break this rule," not "how often throwing happens in
504        production."  Do not use it to gauge live-traffic blast radius without
505        accounting for cache hit rate.
506
507        **Predicates:**
508        - throw_count > 0 and hit_count == 0 → dead-by-exception: the rule
509          has never matched cleanly and throws on every context seen so far.
510        - throw_count > 0 and hit_count > 0 → partial-throw: the rule matches
511          on some inputs but throws on others.  hit_count > 0 does not mean
512          healthy; partial-throw is a distinct broken state.
513        """
514        return dict(self._throw_counts)
515
516    def set_policy(self, new_policy: TarlPolicy):
517        """Replace the active policy and reset the cache and hit counts."""
518        self.policy = new_policy
519        if self._context_schema_origin == "derived":
520            self._context_schema = None
521            self._context_schema_origin = "none"
522        self.cache.clear()
523        self._hit_counts = dict.fromkeys(range(len(new_policy.rules)), 0)
524        self._throw_counts = {}
525
526    # ── Evaluation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
527
528    def evaluate(
529        self,
530        context: dict,
531        policy_text: str | None = None,
532    ) -> TarlDecision:
533        """
534        Evaluate the active policy (or policy_text if supplied) against
535        context. Sources are resolved before evaluation. Returns the
536        first matching rule's verdict, or DEFAULT_DENY.
537        """
538        if policy_text is not None:
539            policy = PolicyParser.parse(policy_text)
540        else:
541            policy = self.policy
542        policy_override = (
543            policy_text is not None and policy.source != self.policy.source
544        )
545        evaluation_schema, schema_resolution_error = self._schema_for_evaluation(
546            policy,
547            policy_override=policy_override,
548        )
549        try:
550            evaluation_now = self._now()
551            if evaluation_now is None:
552                evaluation_now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
553        except ContextResolutionError as exc:
554            return TarlDecision(
555                verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
556                reason=f"fail-closed: {exc}",
557            )
558
559        try:
560            prepared = self._prepare_evaluation_context(context)
561        except ContextResolutionError as exc:
562            return TarlDecision(verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY, reason=str(exc))
563
564        if schema_resolution_error:
565            return TarlDecision(
566                verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
567                reason=f"fail-closed: {schema_resolution_error}",
568            )
569
570        # Context schema validation fails closed before any rule evaluation.
571        schema_decision = self._schema_decision(prepared, evaluation_schema)
572        if schema_decision is not None:
573            return schema_decision
574
575        policy_hash = hashlib.sha256(policy.source.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
576        cache_key = "|".join(
577            (
578                policy_hash,
579                prepared.original_context_hash,
580                prepared.canonical_context_hash,
581                prepared.normalization_algorithm_id,
582                prepared.normalization_version,
583                self._binding_for_schema(
584                    evaluation_schema, "not_evaluated"
585                )["hash"],
586            )
587        )
588
589        # Phase 5: enforce temporal window before any rule evaluation
590        temporal = _check_policy_temporal(policy, now=evaluation_now)
591        if temporal is not None:
592            return temporal
593
594        if not policy.rules:
595            return DEFAULT_DENY
596
597        # Policies with temporal constraints must not be cached — the window
598        # check and expires_at timestamps would be stale on subsequent calls.
599        use_cache = not _is_temporally_constrained(policy)
600
601        if use_cache:
602            cached = self.cache.get(cache_key)
603            if cached is not None:
604                return cached
605
606        ordered_indices = sorted(
607            range(len(policy.rules)),
608            key=lambda i: self._hit_counts.get(i, 0),
609            reverse=True,
610        )
611
612        futures_by_idx = {}
613        trusted_now = evaluation_now
614        for idx in ordered_indices:
615            rule = policy.rules[idx]
616            future = self.executor.submit(
617                self._evaluate_rule, rule, prepared, trusted_now
618            )
619            futures_by_idx[idx] = (future, rule)
620
621        results = {}
622        for idx, (future, rule) in futures_by_idx.items():
623            try:
624                matched, decision, threw = future.result()
625                results[idx] = (matched, decision, rule, threw)
626            except Exception:
627                results[idx] = (
628                    False,
629                    TarlDecision(
630                        verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
631                        reason="Evaluation error",
632                    ),
633                    rule,
634                    True,
635                )
636
637        # Iterate in POLICY ORDER (not hit-count order) to honour
638        # first-match-wins semantics. Adaptive ordering affects which
639        # futures are submitted first, not which result wins.
640        for idx in range(len(policy.rules)):
641            matched, decision, rule, threw = results[idx]
642            if threw:
643                self._throw_counts[idx] = (
644                    self._throw_counts.get(idx, 0) + 1
645                )
646                return TarlDecision(
647                    verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
648                    reason=(
649                        f"fail-closed: rule {idx} could not be evaluated: "
650                        f"{decision.reason}"
651                    ),
652                    rule_index=idx,
653                    matched_rule=str(rule),
654                )
655            if matched:
656                self._hit_counts[idx] = (
657                    self._hit_counts.get(idx, 0) + 1
658                )
659                authority_expiry = _policy_authority_expiry(
660                    policy, rule, trusted_now
661                )
662                expires_at = (
663                    authority_expiry.isoformat(timespec="seconds")
664                    if authority_expiry is not None
665                    else None
666                )
667                result = TarlDecision(
668                    verdict=decision.verdict,
669                    reason=decision.reason or f"Rule matched: {rule}",
670                    rule_index=idx,
671                    matched_rule=str(rule),
672                    expires_at=expires_at,
673                )
674                if use_cache:
675                    self.cache.put(cache_key, result)
676                return result
677
678        if use_cache:
679            self.cache.put(cache_key, DEFAULT_DENY)
680        return DEFAULT_DENY
681
682    def _evaluate_rule(
683        self,
684        rule: TarlRule,
685        context: PreparedContext,
686        now: datetime.datetime | None = None,
687    ) -> tuple:
688        """
689        Evaluate one rule. Returns (matched: bool, TarlDecision, threw: bool).
690
691        threw=True when the condition raised an exception.  The rule is
692        treated as non-matching in either case (fail-safe), but callers
693        increment _throw_counts so persistent exception behaviour is visible
694        via throw_stats().
695        """
696        try:
697            tokens = PolicyParser._tokenize(rule.condition)
698            matched = SafeExpr.evaluate(tokens, context, now=now)
699            if matched:
700                return True, TarlDecision(
701                    verdict=rule.verdict,
702                    reason=f"Condition '{rule.condition}' matched",
703                ), False
704            return False, TarlDecision(
705                verdict=rule.verdict,
706                reason="Condition did not match",
707            ), False
708        except Exception as exc:
709            return False, TarlDecision(
710                verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
711                reason=f"Evaluation error: {exc}",
712            ), True
713
714    # ── Proof-carrying evaluation ─────────────────────────────────────────────
715
716    def evaluate_with_proof(
717        self,
718        context: dict,
719        policy_text: str | None = None,
720    ) -> tuple[TarlDecision, TarlProof]:
721        """
722        Evaluate sequentially, recording a full evaluation trace, then sign.
723
724        Returns (TarlDecision, TarlProof). The proof contains:
725          - SHA-256 hash of policy source
726          - SHA-256 hash of canonical context
727          - Per-rule trace up to (and including) the first match
728          - HMAC-SHA256 or Ed25519 signature if a signing key is registered
729        """
730        if policy_text is not None:
731            policy = PolicyParser.parse(policy_text)
732        else:
733            policy = self.policy
734        policy_override = (
735            policy_text is not None and policy.source != self.policy.source
736        )
737        evaluation_schema, schema_resolution_error = self._schema_for_evaluation(
738            policy,
739            policy_override=policy_override,
740        )
741
742        try:
743            evaluation_now = self._now()
744            if evaluation_now is None:
745                evaluation_now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
746        except ContextResolutionError as exc:
747            try:
748                prepared = prepare_context(context)
749            except ContextResolutionError as context_exc:
750                prepared = rejected_context_binding(
751                    context,
752                    conflict_status=context_exc.conflict_status,
753                )
754            decision = TarlDecision(
755                verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
756                reason=f"fail-closed: {exc}",
757            )
758            trace = [{
759                "kind": "trusted-time-failure",
760                "matched": False,
761                "reason": str(exc),
762                "state": exc.state.value,
763            }]
764            proof = self._generate_proof(
765                policy,
766                prepared,
767                decision,
768                -1,
769                trace,
770                schema_binding=self._binding_for_schema(
771                    evaluation_schema,
772                    "error" if schema_resolution_error else "not_evaluated",
773                ),
774                evaluation_time=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC),
775            )
776            return self._persist(policy, prepared, decision, proof)
777
778        try:
779            prepared = self._prepare_evaluation_context(context)
780        except ContextResolutionError as exc:
781            rejected = rejected_context_binding(
782                context, conflict_status=exc.conflict_status
783            )
784            decision = TarlDecision(verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY, reason=str(exc))
785            trace = [
786                {
787                    "kind": "context-resolution-failure",
788                    "matched": False,
789                    "reason": str(exc),
790                    "state": exc.state.value,
791                }
792            ]
793            proof = self._generate_proof(
794                policy,
795                rejected,
796                decision,
797                -1,
798                trace,
799                schema_binding=self._binding_for_schema(
800                    evaluation_schema,
801                    "error" if schema_resolution_error else "not_evaluated",
802                ),
803                evaluation_time=evaluation_now,
804            )
805            return self._persist(policy, rejected, decision, proof)
806
807        if schema_resolution_error:
808            decision = TarlDecision(
809                verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
810                reason=f"fail-closed: {schema_resolution_error}",
811            )
812            trace = [{
813                "kind": "context-schema-unavailable",
814                "matched": False,
815                "reason": schema_resolution_error,
816            }]
817            proof = self._generate_proof(
818                policy,
819                prepared,
820                decision,
821                -1,
822                trace,
823                schema_binding=self._binding_for_schema(None, "error"),
824                evaluation_time=evaluation_now,
825            )
826            return self._persist(policy, prepared, decision, proof)
827
828        # Context schema validation fails closed before any rule evaluation,
829        # carrying a proof that records which fields were missing or mistyped.
830        schema_decision, schema_binding = self._validate_context_schema(
831            prepared,
832            evaluation_schema,
833        )
834        if schema_decision is not None:
835            trace = [{"kind": "schema-violation", "matched": False,
836                      "reason": schema_decision.reason}]
837            proof = self._generate_proof(
838                policy,
839                prepared,
840                schema_decision,
841                -1,
842                trace,
843                schema_binding=schema_binding,
844                evaluation_time=evaluation_now,
845            )
846            return self._persist(policy, prepared, schema_decision, proof)
847
848        # Phase 5: temporal window check — return early with proof if outside window
849        temporal = _check_policy_temporal(policy, now=evaluation_now)
850        if temporal is not None:
851            proof = self._generate_proof(
852                policy,
853                prepared,
854                temporal,
855                -1,
856                [],
857                schema_binding=schema_binding,
858                evaluation_time=evaluation_now,
859            )
860            return self._persist(policy, prepared, temporal, proof)
861
862        trace = []
863        decision = DEFAULT_DENY
864        matched_idx = -1
865        trusted_now = evaluation_now
866
867        for i, rule in enumerate(policy.rules):
868            matched, rule_dec, threw = self._evaluate_rule(
869                rule, prepared, trusted_now
870            )
871            if threw:
872                self._throw_counts[i] = (
873                    self._throw_counts.get(i, 0) + 1
874                )
875            trace.append({
876                **({"kind": "evaluation-error"} if threw else {}),
877                "rule_index": i,
878                "condition": rule.condition,
879                "verdict": rule.verdict.value,
880                "matched": matched,
881                **({"error": rule_dec.reason} if threw else {}),
882            })
883            if threw:
884                decision = TarlDecision(
885                    verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
886                    reason=(
887                        f"fail-closed: rule {i} could not be evaluated: "
888                        f"{rule_dec.reason}"
889                    ),
890                    rule_index=i,
891                    matched_rule=str(rule),
892                )
893                matched_idx = -1
894                break
895            if matched:
896                matched_idx = i
897                authority_expiry = _policy_authority_expiry(
898                    policy, rule, trusted_now
899                )
900                expires_at = (
901                    authority_expiry.isoformat(timespec="seconds")
902                    if authority_expiry is not None
903                    else None
904                )
905                decision = TarlDecision(
906                    verdict=rule_dec.verdict,
907                    reason=f"Condition '{rule.condition}' matched",
908                    rule_index=i,
909                    matched_rule=str(rule),
910                    expires_at=expires_at,
911                )
912                break
913
914        proof = self._generate_proof(
915            policy,
916            prepared,
917            decision,
918            matched_idx,
919            trace,
920            schema_binding=schema_binding,
921            evaluation_time=evaluation_now,
922        )
923        return self._persist(policy, prepared, decision, proof)
924
925    def _generate_proof(
926        self,
927        policy: TarlPolicy,
928        context: PreparedContext,
929        decision: TarlDecision,
930        matched_idx: int,
931        trace: list,
932        schema_binding: dict[str, str] | None = None,
933        evaluation_time: datetime.datetime | None = None,
934    ) -> TarlProof:
935        policy_hash = "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(
936            policy.source.encode("utf-8")
937        ).hexdigest()
938        context_hash = (
939            context.canonical_context_hash or context.original_context_hash
940        )
941        if evaluation_time is None:
942            evaluation_time = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
943        if (
944            evaluation_time.tzinfo is None
945            or evaluation_time.utcoffset() is None
946        ):
947            raise ValueError("proof evaluation time must be timezone-aware")
948        evaluated_at = (
949            evaluation_time.astimezone(datetime.UTC)
950            .isoformat(timespec="seconds")
951            .replace("+00:00", "Z")
952        )
953        matched_condition = (
954            policy.rules[matched_idx].condition if matched_idx >= 0 else ""
955        )
956        schema_binding = schema_binding or self._schema_binding("not_evaluated")
957        proof = TarlProof(
958            policy_hash=policy_hash,
959            context_hash=context_hash,
960            rule_index=matched_idx,
961            matched_condition=matched_condition,
962            verdict=decision.verdict,
963            evaluated_at=evaluated_at,
964            trace=trace,
965            signature="",
966            key_id="",
967            original_context_hash=context.original_context_hash,
968            canonical_context_hash=context.canonical_context_hash,
969            context_representation_id=context.context_representation_id,
970            normalization_algorithm_id=context.normalization_algorithm_id,
971            normalization_version=context.normalization_version,
972            context_conflict_status=context.context_conflict_status,
973            context_schema_hash=schema_binding["hash"],
974            context_schema_representation_id=(
975                schema_binding["representation_id"]
976            ),
977            context_schema_validation_status=schema_binding["status"],
978            expires_at=decision.expires_at,
979        )
980        if self._signing_key_id and self._signing_alg == "hmac-sha256":
981            secret = self._signing_keys.get(self._signing_key_id)
982            if secret is not None:
983                sig_hex = hmac.new(
984                    secret, proof.canonical_bytes(), hashlib.sha256
985                ).hexdigest()
986                proof.signature = f"hmac-sha256:{sig_hex}"
987                proof.key_id = self._signing_key_id
988        elif self._signing_key_id and self._signing_alg == "ed25519":
989            key = self._ed25519_signing_keys.get(self._signing_key_id)
990            if key is not None:
991                sig_hex = key.sign(proof.canonical_bytes()).hex()
992                proof.signature = f"ed25519:{sig_hex}"
993                proof.key_id = self._signing_key_id
994        return proof
995
996    def shutdown(self):
997        """Clean up the thread pool."""
998        self.executor.shutdown(wait=False)

TARL policy runtime:

  • LRU decision cache (128 entries)
  • ThreadPoolExecutor for parallel rule evaluation
  • Adaptive ordering (most-frequently-matched rules evaluated first)
  • Dynamic source registry for source:name condition references
TarlRuntime(policy: TarlPolicy | None = None, max_workers: int = 4) 
108    def __init__(
109        self,
110        policy: TarlPolicy | None = None,
111        max_workers: int = 4,
112    ):
113        self.policy = policy or TarlPolicy()
114        self.cache = LRUCache(maxsize=128)
115        self.executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers)
116        self._hit_counts: dict = {}
117        self._throw_counts: dict = {}   # rule_index -> number of evaluation exceptions
118        self._sources: dict = {}
119        self._signing_keys: dict = {}   # key_id -> bytes (HMAC secrets)
120        self._ed25519_signing_keys: dict = {}  # key_id -> Ed25519PrivateKey
121        self._signing_key_id: str = ""  # active key
122        self._signing_alg: str = ""     # "hmac-sha256" or "ed25519"
123        self._archive = None            # TarlAuditArchive | None
124        self._context_schema: ContextSchema | None = None
125        self._context_schema_origin = "none"
126        self._require_audit = False     # fail closed if audit cannot persist
127        # Trusted time source for temporal checks; None => host clock.
128        self._clock: Callable[[], datetime.datetime | None] | None = None
policy
cache
executor
def set_clock(self, clock) -> TarlRuntime: 
130    def set_clock(self, clock) -> "TarlRuntime":
131        """Use a trusted time source for temporal-policy checks instead of the
132        host clock. ``clock`` is a zero-arg callable returning a timezone-aware
133        ``datetime`` (typically obtained by verifying a signed-time assertion via
134        ``utf.tarl.clock.TrustedClock``). A spoofed system clock then cannot
135        satisfy a temporal window (C043). Returns self."""
136        if not callable(clock):
137            raise TypeError("clock must be callable")
138        self._clock = clock
139        return self

Use a trusted time source for temporal-policy checks instead of the host clock. clock is a zero-arg callable returning a timezone-aware datetime (typically obtained by verifying a signed-time assertion via utf.tarl.clock.TrustedClock). A spoofed system clock then cannot satisfy a temporal window (C043). Returns self.

def set_require_audit(self, required: bool = True) -> TarlRuntime: 
163    def set_require_audit(self, required: bool = True) -> "TarlRuntime":
164        """When True and an audit archive is attached, a failure to persist a

When True and an audit archive is attached, a failure to persist a proof downgrades the decision to a fail-closed DENY (C038): execution cannot proceed if the required audit record could not be written.

def set_context_schema( self, schema: utf.tarl.schema.ContextSchema) -> TarlRuntime: 
212    def set_context_schema(self, schema: ContextSchema) -> "TarlRuntime":
213        """Attach a ``utf.tarl.schema.ContextSchema``. When set, every context is
214        validated before any rule runs; a missing required field or a
215        type-confused value short-circuits to the schema's fail-closed verdict
216        (DENY by default) instead of silently matching a permissive later rule.
217        Returns self for chaining."""
218        if type(schema) is not ContextSchema:
219            raise TypeError("context schema must be a ContextSchema")
220        # Validate and fingerprint at registration time so malformed schema
221        # configuration cannot reach an authorization path.
222        schema.fingerprint()
223        self._context_schema = schema
224        self._context_schema_origin = "explicit"
225        return self

Attach a utf.tarl.schema.ContextSchema. When set, every context is validated before any rule runs; a missing required field or a type-confused value short-circuits to the schema's fail-closed verdict (DENY by default) instead of silently matching a permissive later rule. Returns self for chaining.

def ensure_context_schema(self) -> bool: 
227    def ensure_context_schema(self) -> bool:
228        """Attach a complete derived schema when authority use needs one.
229
230        Plain evaluation remains available without a schema, but load-bearing
231        consumers call this method before relying on ALLOW.  Incomplete or
232        ambiguous derivation leaves the runtime unbound so the consumer's
233        positive-proof admissibility gate fails closed.
234        """
235        if self._context_schema is not None:
236            return True
237        try:
238            from utf.thirsty_lang.proof_obligations import derive_context_schema
239
240            derived = derive_context_schema(self.policy.source)
241            if not derived.complete:
242                return False
243            self.set_context_schema(ContextSchema.from_dict(derived.to_dict()))
244            self._context_schema_origin = "derived"
245        except Exception:
246            return False
247        return True

Attach a complete derived schema when authority use needs one.

Plain evaluation remains available without a schema, but load-bearing consumers call this method before relying on ALLOW. Incomplete or ambiguous derivation leaves the runtime unbound so the consumer's positive-proof admissibility gate fails closed.

394        self._archive = archive

399    def set_signing_key(
400        self, key_id: str, secret: bytes
401    ) -> "TarlRuntime":
402        """
403        Register an HMAC-SHA256 signing key for proof generation.
404        The most recently set key becomes the active key.
405        Returns self for chaining.
406        """
407        self._signing_keys[key_id] = secret
408        self._signing_key_id = key_id
409        self._signing_alg = "hmac-sha256"
410        return self

Register an HMAC-SHA256 signing key for proof generation. The most recently set key becomes the active key. Returns self for chaining.

def set_ed25519_signing_key( self, key_id: str, private_key: bytes | cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519.Ed25519PrivateKey) -> TarlRuntime: 
412    def set_ed25519_signing_key(
413        self, key_id: str, private_key: bytes | Ed25519PrivateKey
414    ) -> "TarlRuntime":
415        """
416        Register an Ed25519 private key for proof generation.
417
418        ``private_key`` may be a cryptography Ed25519PrivateKey or the raw
419        32-byte private seed accepted by Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes().
420        The most recently set key becomes the active key.
421        """
422        if isinstance(private_key, Ed25519PrivateKey):
423            key = private_key
424        else:
425            key = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(private_key)
426        self._ed25519_signing_keys[key_id] = key
427        self._signing_key_id = key_id
428        self._signing_alg = "ed25519"
429        return self

Register an Ed25519 private key for proof generation.

private_key may be a cryptography Ed25519PrivateKey or the raw 32-byte private seed accepted by Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(). The most recently set key becomes the active key.

def register_source(self, name: str, provider) -> TarlRuntime: 
433    def register_source(
434        self, name: str, provider
435    ) -> "TarlRuntime":
436        """
437        Bind a data provider to source:<name> condition references.
438
439        provider — a strict JSON value (commonly a list) or a zero-arg
440                   callable that returns one each time it is called.
441        Returns self for chaining.
442        """
443        if (
444            type(name) is not str
445            or not name
446            or not all(char.isalnum() or char == "_" for char in name)
447        ):
448            raise ValueError(
449                "registered source name must be non-empty and contain only "
450                "letters, numbers, or underscores"
451            )
452        self._sources[name] = provider
453        return self

def throw_stats(self) -> dict: 
494    def throw_stats(self) -> dict:
495        """
496        Return throw counts per rule index.
497
498        **What the number means:**
499        Counts reflect distinct contexts that missed the cache and threw, not
500        total call frequency.  A rule that throws on one bad context evaluated
501        a thousand times shows throw_count == 1, not 1000, because cached
502        results bypass rule evaluation entirely.  The stat answers "how many
503        distinct inputs break this rule," not "how often throwing happens in
504        production."  Do not use it to gauge live-traffic blast radius without
505        accounting for cache hit rate.
506
507        **Predicates:**
508        - throw_count > 0 and hit_count == 0 → dead-by-exception: the rule
509          has never matched cleanly and throws on every context seen so far.
510        - throw_count > 0 and hit_count > 0 → partial-throw: the rule matches
511          on some inputs but throws on others.  hit_count > 0 does not mean
512          healthy; partial-throw is a distinct broken state.
513        """
514        return dict(self._throw_counts)

Return throw counts per rule index.

What the number means: Counts reflect distinct contexts that missed the cache and threw, not total call frequency. A rule that throws on one bad context evaluated a thousand times shows throw_count == 1, not 1000, because cached results bypass rule evaluation entirely. The stat answers "how many distinct inputs break this rule," not "how often throwing happens in production." Do not use it to gauge live-traffic blast radius without accounting for cache hit rate.

Predicates:

  • throw_count > 0 and hit_count == 0 → dead-by-exception: the rule has never matched cleanly and throws on every context seen so far.
  • throw_count > 0 and hit_count > 0 → partial-throw: the rule matches on some inputs but throws on others. hit_count > 0 does not mean healthy; partial-throw is a distinct broken state.
def set_policy(self, new_policy: TarlPolicy): 
516    def set_policy(self, new_policy: TarlPolicy):
517        """Replace the active policy and reset the cache and hit counts."""
518        self.policy = new_policy
519        if self._context_schema_origin == "derived":
520            self._context_schema = None
521            self._context_schema_origin = "none"
522        self.cache.clear()
523        self._hit_counts = dict.fromkeys(range(len(new_policy.rules)), 0)
524        self._throw_counts = {}

Replace the active policy and reset the cache and hit counts.

def evaluate( self, context: dict, policy_text: str | None = None) -> TarlDecision: 
528    def evaluate(
529        self,
530        context: dict,
531        policy_text: str | None = None,
532    ) -> TarlDecision:
533        """
534        Evaluate the active policy (or policy_text if supplied) against
535        context. Sources are resolved before evaluation. Returns the
536        first matching rule's verdict, or DEFAULT_DENY.
537        """
538        if policy_text is not None:
539            policy = PolicyParser.parse(policy_text)
540        else:
541            policy = self.policy
542        policy_override = (
543            policy_text is not None and policy.source != self.policy.source
544        )
545        evaluation_schema, schema_resolution_error = self._schema_for_evaluation(
546            policy,
547            policy_override=policy_override,
548        )
549        try:
550            evaluation_now = self._now()
551            if evaluation_now is None:
552                evaluation_now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
553        except ContextResolutionError as exc:
554            return TarlDecision(
555                verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
556                reason=f"fail-closed: {exc}",
557            )
558
559        try:
560            prepared = self._prepare_evaluation_context(context)
561        except ContextResolutionError as exc:
562            return TarlDecision(verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY, reason=str(exc))
563
564        if schema_resolution_error:
565            return TarlDecision(
566                verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
567                reason=f"fail-closed: {schema_resolution_error}",
568            )
569
570        # Context schema validation fails closed before any rule evaluation.
571        schema_decision = self._schema_decision(prepared, evaluation_schema)
572        if schema_decision is not None:
573            return schema_decision
574
575        policy_hash = hashlib.sha256(policy.source.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
576        cache_key = "|".join(
577            (
578                policy_hash,
579                prepared.original_context_hash,
580                prepared.canonical_context_hash,
581                prepared.normalization_algorithm_id,
582                prepared.normalization_version,
583                self._binding_for_schema(
584                    evaluation_schema, "not_evaluated"
585                )["hash"],
586            )
587        )
588
589        # Phase 5: enforce temporal window before any rule evaluation
590        temporal = _check_policy_temporal(policy, now=evaluation_now)
591        if temporal is not None:
592            return temporal
593
594        if not policy.rules:
595            return DEFAULT_DENY
596
597        # Policies with temporal constraints must not be cached — the window
598        # check and expires_at timestamps would be stale on subsequent calls.
599        use_cache = not _is_temporally_constrained(policy)
600
601        if use_cache:
602            cached = self.cache.get(cache_key)
603            if cached is not None:
604                return cached
605
606        ordered_indices = sorted(
607            range(len(policy.rules)),
608            key=lambda i: self._hit_counts.get(i, 0),
609            reverse=True,
610        )
611
612        futures_by_idx = {}
613        trusted_now = evaluation_now
614        for idx in ordered_indices:
615            rule = policy.rules[idx]
616            future = self.executor.submit(
617                self._evaluate_rule, rule, prepared, trusted_now
618            )
619            futures_by_idx[idx] = (future, rule)
620
621        results = {}
622        for idx, (future, rule) in futures_by_idx.items():
623            try:
624                matched, decision, threw = future.result()
625                results[idx] = (matched, decision, rule, threw)
626            except Exception:
627                results[idx] = (
628                    False,
629                    TarlDecision(
630                        verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
631                        reason="Evaluation error",
632                    ),
633                    rule,
634                    True,
635                )
636
637        # Iterate in POLICY ORDER (not hit-count order) to honour
638        # first-match-wins semantics. Adaptive ordering affects which
639        # futures are submitted first, not which result wins.
640        for idx in range(len(policy.rules)):
641            matched, decision, rule, threw = results[idx]
642            if threw:
643                self._throw_counts[idx] = (
644                    self._throw_counts.get(idx, 0) + 1
645                )
646                return TarlDecision(
647                    verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
648                    reason=(
649                        f"fail-closed: rule {idx} could not be evaluated: "
650                        f"{decision.reason}"
651                    ),
652                    rule_index=idx,
653                    matched_rule=str(rule),
654                )
655            if matched:
656                self._hit_counts[idx] = (
657                    self._hit_counts.get(idx, 0) + 1
658                )
659                authority_expiry = _policy_authority_expiry(
660                    policy, rule, trusted_now
661                )
662                expires_at = (
663                    authority_expiry.isoformat(timespec="seconds")
664                    if authority_expiry is not None
665                    else None
666                )
667                result = TarlDecision(
668                    verdict=decision.verdict,
669                    reason=decision.reason or f"Rule matched: {rule}",
670                    rule_index=idx,
671                    matched_rule=str(rule),
672                    expires_at=expires_at,
673                )
674                if use_cache:
675                    self.cache.put(cache_key, result)
676                return result
677
678        if use_cache:
679            self.cache.put(cache_key, DEFAULT_DENY)
680        return DEFAULT_DENY

Evaluate the active policy (or policy_text if supplied) against context. Sources are resolved before evaluation. Returns the first matching rule's verdict, or DEFAULT_DENY.

def evaluate_with_proof( self, context: dict, policy_text: str | None = None) -> tuple[TarlDecision, TarlProof]: 
716    def evaluate_with_proof(
717        self,
718        context: dict,
719        policy_text: str | None = None,
720    ) -> tuple[TarlDecision, TarlProof]:
721        """
722        Evaluate sequentially, recording a full evaluation trace, then sign.
723
724        Returns (TarlDecision, TarlProof). The proof contains:
725          - SHA-256 hash of policy source
726          - SHA-256 hash of canonical context
727          - Per-rule trace up to (and including) the first match
728          - HMAC-SHA256 or Ed25519 signature if a signing key is registered
729        """
730        if policy_text is not None:
731            policy = PolicyParser.parse(policy_text)
732        else:
733            policy = self.policy
734        policy_override = (
735            policy_text is not None and policy.source != self.policy.source
736        )
737        evaluation_schema, schema_resolution_error = self._schema_for_evaluation(
738            policy,
739            policy_override=policy_override,
740        )
741
742        try:
743            evaluation_now = self._now()
744            if evaluation_now is None:
745                evaluation_now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
746        except ContextResolutionError as exc:
747            try:
748                prepared = prepare_context(context)
749            except ContextResolutionError as context_exc:
750                prepared = rejected_context_binding(
751                    context,
752                    conflict_status=context_exc.conflict_status,
753                )
754            decision = TarlDecision(
755                verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
756                reason=f"fail-closed: {exc}",
757            )
758            trace = [{
759                "kind": "trusted-time-failure",
760                "matched": False,
761                "reason": str(exc),
762                "state": exc.state.value,
763            }]
764            proof = self._generate_proof(
765                policy,
766                prepared,
767                decision,
768                -1,
769                trace,
770                schema_binding=self._binding_for_schema(
771                    evaluation_schema,
772                    "error" if schema_resolution_error else "not_evaluated",
773                ),
774                evaluation_time=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC),
775            )
776            return self._persist(policy, prepared, decision, proof)
777
778        try:
779            prepared = self._prepare_evaluation_context(context)
780        except ContextResolutionError as exc:
781            rejected = rejected_context_binding(
782                context, conflict_status=exc.conflict_status
783            )
784            decision = TarlDecision(verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY, reason=str(exc))
785            trace = [
786                {
787                    "kind": "context-resolution-failure",
788                    "matched": False,
789                    "reason": str(exc),
790                    "state": exc.state.value,
791                }
792            ]
793            proof = self._generate_proof(
794                policy,
795                rejected,
796                decision,
797                -1,
798                trace,
799                schema_binding=self._binding_for_schema(
800                    evaluation_schema,
801                    "error" if schema_resolution_error else "not_evaluated",
802                ),
803                evaluation_time=evaluation_now,
804            )
805            return self._persist(policy, rejected, decision, proof)
806
807        if schema_resolution_error:
808            decision = TarlDecision(
809                verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
810                reason=f"fail-closed: {schema_resolution_error}",
811            )
812            trace = [{
813                "kind": "context-schema-unavailable",
814                "matched": False,
815                "reason": schema_resolution_error,
816            }]
817            proof = self._generate_proof(
818                policy,
819                prepared,
820                decision,
821                -1,
822                trace,
823                schema_binding=self._binding_for_schema(None, "error"),
824                evaluation_time=evaluation_now,
825            )
826            return self._persist(policy, prepared, decision, proof)
827
828        # Context schema validation fails closed before any rule evaluation,
829        # carrying a proof that records which fields were missing or mistyped.
830        schema_decision, schema_binding = self._validate_context_schema(
831            prepared,
832            evaluation_schema,
833        )
834        if schema_decision is not None:
835            trace = [{"kind": "schema-violation", "matched": False,
836                      "reason": schema_decision.reason}]
837            proof = self._generate_proof(
838                policy,
839                prepared,
840                schema_decision,
841                -1,
842                trace,
843                schema_binding=schema_binding,
844                evaluation_time=evaluation_now,
845            )
846            return self._persist(policy, prepared, schema_decision, proof)
847
848        # Phase 5: temporal window check — return early with proof if outside window
849        temporal = _check_policy_temporal(policy, now=evaluation_now)
850        if temporal is not None:
851            proof = self._generate_proof(
852                policy,
853                prepared,
854                temporal,
855                -1,
856                [],
857                schema_binding=schema_binding,
858                evaluation_time=evaluation_now,
859            )
860            return self._persist(policy, prepared, temporal, proof)
861
862        trace = []
863        decision = DEFAULT_DENY
864        matched_idx = -1
865        trusted_now = evaluation_now
866
867        for i, rule in enumerate(policy.rules):
868            matched, rule_dec, threw = self._evaluate_rule(
869                rule, prepared, trusted_now
870            )
871            if threw:
872                self._throw_counts[i] = (
873                    self._throw_counts.get(i, 0) + 1
874                )
875            trace.append({
876                **({"kind": "evaluation-error"} if threw else {}),
877                "rule_index": i,
878                "condition": rule.condition,
879                "verdict": rule.verdict.value,
880                "matched": matched,
881                **({"error": rule_dec.reason} if threw else {}),
882            })
883            if threw:
884                decision = TarlDecision(
885                    verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
886                    reason=(
887                        f"fail-closed: rule {i} could not be evaluated: "
888                        f"{rule_dec.reason}"
889                    ),
890                    rule_index=i,
891                    matched_rule=str(rule),
892                )
893                matched_idx = -1
894                break
895            if matched:
896                matched_idx = i
897                authority_expiry = _policy_authority_expiry(
898                    policy, rule, trusted_now
899                )
900                expires_at = (
901                    authority_expiry.isoformat(timespec="seconds")
902                    if authority_expiry is not None
903                    else None
904                )
905                decision = TarlDecision(
906                    verdict=rule_dec.verdict,
907                    reason=f"Condition '{rule.condition}' matched",
908                    rule_index=i,
909                    matched_rule=str(rule),
910                    expires_at=expires_at,
911                )
912                break
913
914        proof = self._generate_proof(
915            policy,
916            prepared,
917            decision,
918            matched_idx,
919            trace,
920            schema_binding=schema_binding,
921            evaluation_time=evaluation_now,
922        )
923        return self._persist(policy, prepared, decision, proof)

Evaluate sequentially, recording a full evaluation trace, then sign.

Returns (TarlDecision, TarlProof). The proof contains:

  • SHA-256 hash of policy source
  • SHA-256 hash of canonical context
  • Per-rule trace up to (and including) the first match
