class PolicyComposer: 
 39class PolicyComposer:
 40    """
 41    Registry and evaluator for composed T.A.R.L. policies.
 42
 43    Phase 5: temporal window enforcement and policy succession (revert_to)
 44    are applied automatically before EXTENDS/RESTRICTS dispatch.
 45
 46    Usage:
 47        composer = PolicyComposer()
 48        composer.register(base_policy)
 49        composer.register(child_policy)   # child EXTENDS base
 50        decision = composer.evaluate("child", context)
 51    """
 52
 53    def __init__(self, base_path: str = "."):
 54        self._policies: dict[str, TarlPolicy] = {}
 55        self._sets: dict[str, TarlPolicySet] = {}
 56        self._base_path = base_path
 57
 58    # ── Registration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 59
 60    def register(self, policy: TarlPolicy) -> PolicyComposer:
 61        """Register a TarlPolicy by name. Returns self for chaining."""
 62        self._policies[policy.name] = policy
 63        return self
 64
 65    def register_set(self, policy_set: TarlPolicySet) -> PolicyComposer:
 66        """Register a TarlPolicySet by name. Returns self for chaining."""
 67        self._sets[policy_set.name] = policy_set
 68        return self
 69
 70    def register_from_text(
 71        self, text: str, name: str | None = None
 72    ) -> PolicyComposer:
 73        """
 74        Parse text and register all policies and policy_sets it contains.
 75        Returns self for chaining.
 76        """
 77        from utf.tarl.core import PolicyParser
 78
 79        items = PolicyParser.parse_all(text)
 80        for item in items:
 81            if isinstance(item, TarlPolicySet):
 82                self._sets[item.name] = item
 83            elif isinstance(item, TarlPolicy):
 84                if name and len(items) == 1 and item.name == "unnamed":
 85                    item.name = name
 86                self._policies[item.name] = item
 87        return self
 88
 89    def load_file(self, path: str) -> PolicyComposer:
 90        """
 91        Read a .tarl file and register everything it contains.
 92        Paths are resolved relative to self._base_path.
 93        Returns self for chaining.
 94        """
 95        full = (
 96            path if os.path.isabs(path)
 97            else os.path.join(self._base_path, path)
 98        )
 99        with open(full, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
100            return self.register_from_text(fh.read())
101
102    def names(self) -> list[str]:
103        """All registered policy names."""
104        return list(self._policies.keys())
105
106    def set_names(self) -> list[str]:
107        """All registered policy_set names."""
108        return list(self._sets.keys())
109
110    # ── Public evaluation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
111
112    def evaluate(self, name: str, context: dict) -> TarlDecision:
113        """
114        Evaluate a named policy or policy_set against context.
115        Raises CompositionError if the name is not registered.
116        """
117        if name in self._sets:
118            return self._evaluate_set(name, context)
119        if name in self._policies:
120            return self._evaluate_policy(
121                self._policies[name], context, frozenset()
122            )
123        registered = sorted(self._policies) + sorted(self._sets)
124        raise CompositionError(
125            f"Unknown policy or policy_set: {name!r}. "
126            f"Registered: {registered}"
127        )
128
129    # ── Internal policy evaluation ────────────────────────────────────────────
130
131    def _evaluate_policy(
132        self,
133        policy: TarlPolicy,
134        context: dict,
135        chain: frozenset[str],
136    ) -> TarlDecision:
137        """Dispatch to the correct composition handler."""
138        from utf.tarl.core import _check_policy_temporal, evaluate_policy
139
140        # Phase 5: temporal window check before any rule evaluation.
141        # If the policy has a revert_to target registered in this composer,
142        # evaluate that policy instead (succession). Otherwise return the
143        # on_expiry verdict (or ESCALATE).
144        temporal = _check_policy_temporal(policy)
145        if temporal is not None:
146            if policy.revert_to and policy.revert_to in self._policies:
147                # Guard against succession cycles (A→B→A) using the same
148                # chain mechanism as EXTENDS/RESTRICTS.
149                self._check_cycle(policy.name, chain)
150                revert_policy = self._policies[policy.revert_to]
151                return self._evaluate_policy(
152                    revert_policy, context, chain | {policy.name}
153                )
154            return temporal
155
156        # Pre-evaluate INCLUDE directives, inject into context copy
157        ctx = dict(context)
158        if policy.includes:
159            try:
160                ctx = self._inject_includes(policy.includes, ctx, chain)
161            except ContextResolutionError as exc:
162                return TarlDecision(verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY, reason=str(exc))
163
164        if policy.composition == CompositionOp.EXTENDS:
165            return self._evaluate_extends(policy, ctx, chain)
166        if policy.composition == CompositionOp.RESTRICTS:
167            return self._evaluate_restricts(policy, ctx, chain)
168
169        return evaluate_policy(ctx, policy=policy)
170
171    def _evaluate_extends(
172        self,
173        policy: TarlPolicy,
174        context: dict,
175        chain: frozenset[str],
176    ) -> TarlDecision:
177        """
178        EXTENDS semantics:
179          1. Evaluate child rules only.
180          2. If a child rule matched → return that decision.
181          3. If STOP is set → return DEFAULT_DENY (no parent fallthrough).
182          4. Otherwise → fall through to parent rules.
183        """
184        from utf.tarl.core import evaluate_policy
185
186        self._check_cycle(policy.name, chain)
187
188        child_only = TarlPolicy(
189            rules=list(policy.rules),
190            name=policy.name,
191        )
192        decision = evaluate_policy(context, policy=child_only)
193
194        if decision.rule_index >= 0:
195            return decision
196
197        if policy.has_stop:
198            return DEFAULT_DENY
199
200        if not policy.parent:
201            return DEFAULT_DENY
202
203        parent = self._require(policy.parent, policy.name)
204        return self._evaluate_policy(
205            parent, context, chain | {policy.name}
206        )
207
208    def _evaluate_restricts(
209        self,
210        policy: TarlPolicy,
211        context: dict,
212        chain: frozenset[str],
213    ) -> TarlDecision:
214        """
215        RESTRICTS semantics:
216          Evaluate child and parent independently.
217          Final verdict = meet(child, parent) — stricter wins.
218        """
219        from utf.tarl.core import evaluate_policy
220
221        self._check_cycle(policy.name, chain)
222
223        child_only = TarlPolicy(
224            rules=list(policy.rules),
225            name=policy.name,
226        )
227        child_dec = evaluate_policy(context, policy=child_only)
228
229        parent = self._require(policy.parent, policy.name)
230        parent_dec = self._evaluate_policy(
231            parent, context, chain | {policy.name}
232        )
233
234        meet = TarlVerdict.meet(child_dec.verdict, parent_dec.verdict)
235        src = child_dec if meet == child_dec.verdict else parent_dec
236        return TarlDecision(
237            verdict=meet,
238            reason=(
239                f"RESTRICTS({policy.parent}): "
240                f"child={child_dec.verdict.value}, "
241                f"parent={parent_dec.verdict.value}"
242            ),
243            rule_index=src.rule_index,
244            matched_rule=src.matched_rule,
245        )
246
247    def _inject_includes(
248        self,
249        refs: list[TarlPolicyRef],
250        context: dict,
251        chain: frozenset[str],
252    ) -> dict:
253        """
254        Pre-evaluate each INCLUDE'd policy and inject its verdict into ctx.
255
256        Injects one nested object per include:
257          ctx["<alias>"] = {"verdict": "<VERDICT>", "rule_index": <int>}
258
259        ``alias.verdict`` in a policy is a path into that object. A second flat
260        dotted key would be a conflicting context representation and is never
261        synthesized.
262        """
263        ctx = dict(context)
264        for ref in refs:
265            alias = ref.alias or ref.name
266
267            # Resolve file-based includes
268            policy_name = ref.name
269            if ref.is_file:
270                stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(ref.name))[0]
271                if stem not in self._policies:
272                    try:
273                        self.load_file(ref.name)
274                    except OSError:
275                        ctx = compose_context_layers(
276                            ("composition context", ctx),
277                            (f"include '{alias}'", {
278                                alias: {"verdict": "DENY", "rule_index": -1}
279                            }),
280                        )
281                        continue
282                policy_name = stem
283
284            if policy_name not in self._policies:
285                ctx = compose_context_layers(
286                    ("composition context", ctx),
287                    (f"include '{alias}'", {
288                        alias: {"verdict": "DENY", "rule_index": -1}
289                    }),
290                )
291                continue
292
293            inc_policy = self._policies[policy_name]
294            inc_dec = self._evaluate_policy(inc_policy, ctx, chain)
295            ctx = compose_context_layers(
296                ("composition context", ctx),
297                (f"include '{alias}'", {
298                    alias: {
299                        "verdict": inc_dec.verdict.value,
300                        "rule_index": inc_dec.rule_index,
301                    }
302                }),
303            )
304
305        return ctx
306
307    # ── Policy-set evaluation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
308
309    def _evaluate_set(self, name: str, context: dict) -> TarlDecision:
310        """
311        policy_set evaluation:
312          Each group produces a verdict via its SetOp.
313          The final verdict is the meet (∧) of all group verdicts.
314          If no groups are defined, the set's default_verdict is returned.
315        """
316        ps = self._sets[name]
317
318        if not ps.groups:
319            return TarlDecision(
320                verdict=ps.default_verdict,
321                reason=f"policy_set {name}: no groups defined",
322            )
323
324        group_verdicts: list[TarlVerdict] = []
325        group_summaries: list[str] = []
326
327        for op, policy_names in ps.groups:
328            dec = self._evaluate_group(op, policy_names, context)
329            group_verdicts.append(dec.verdict)
330            group_summaries.append(f"{op.value}={dec.verdict.value}")
331
332        final = group_verdicts[0]
333        for v in group_verdicts[1:]:
334            final = TarlVerdict.meet(final, v)
335
336        return TarlDecision(
337            verdict=final,
338            reason=f"policy_set {name}: " + ", ".join(group_summaries),
339        )
340
341    def _evaluate_group(
342        self,
343        op: SetOp,
344        policy_names: list[str],
345        context: dict,
346    ) -> TarlDecision:
347        """Evaluate a single combine group using the given operator."""
348        verdicts: list[TarlVerdict] = []
349        for pname in policy_names:
350            if pname in self._policies:
351                dec = self._evaluate_policy(
352                    self._policies[pname], context, frozenset()
353                )
354                verdicts.append(dec.verdict)
355            else:
356                verdicts.append(TarlVerdict.DENY)
357
358        if not verdicts:
359            return TarlDecision(
360                verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
361                reason=f"{op.value}: empty group",
362            )
363
364        if op == SetOp.UNION:
365            result = verdicts[0]
366            for v in verdicts[1:]:
367                result = TarlVerdict.join(result, v)
368        elif op == SetOp.INTERSECT:
369            result = verdicts[0]
370            for v in verdicts[1:]:
371                result = TarlVerdict.meet(result, v)
372        elif op == SetOp.MAJORITY:
373            allow_count = sum(
374                1 for v in verdicts if v == TarlVerdict.ALLOW
375            )
376            result = (
377                TarlVerdict.ALLOW
378                if allow_count > len(verdicts) / 2
379                else TarlVerdict.DENY
380            )
381        else:
382            result = TarlVerdict.DENY
383
384        return TarlDecision(
385            verdict=result,
386            reason=(
387                f"{op.value}("
388                + ", ".join(v.value for v in verdicts)
389                + f") = {result.value}"
390            ),
391        )
392
393    # ── Helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
394
395    def _require(self, name: str | None, from_name: str) -> TarlPolicy:
396        if name is None or name not in self._policies:
397            raise CompositionError(
398                f"Policy {from_name!r} references unknown policy "
399                f"{name!r}. Registered: {sorted(self._policies.keys())}"
400            )
401        return self._policies[name]
402
403    def _check_cycle(self, name: str, chain: frozenset[str]) -> None:
404        if name in chain:
405            path = " -> ".join(sorted(chain)) + f" -> {name}"
406            raise CompositionError(
407                f"Circular policy reference detected: {path}"
408            )

Registry and evaluator for composed T.A.R.L. policies.

Phase 5: temporal window enforcement and policy succession (revert_to) are applied automatically before EXTENDS/RESTRICTS dispatch.

Usage: composer = PolicyComposer() composer.register(base_policy) composer.register(child_policy) # child EXTENDS base decision = composer.evaluate("child", context)

70    def register_from_text(
71        self, text: str, name: str | None = None
72    ) -> PolicyComposer:
73        """
74        Parse text and register all policies and policy_sets it contains.
75        Returns self for chaining.
76        """
77        from utf.tarl.core import PolicyParser
78
79        items = PolicyParser.parse_all(text)
80        for item in items:
81            if isinstance(item, TarlPolicySet):
82                self._sets[item.name] = item
83            elif isinstance(item, TarlPolicy):
84                if name and len(items) == 1 and item.name == "unnamed":
85                    item.name = name
86                self._policies[item.name] = item
87        return self

112    def evaluate(self, name: str, context: dict) -> TarlDecision:
113        """
114        Evaluate a named policy or policy_set against context.
115        Raises CompositionError if the name is not registered.
116        """
117        if name in self._sets:
118            return self._evaluate_set(name, context)
119        if name in self._policies:
120            return self._evaluate_policy(
121                self._policies[name], context, frozenset()
122            )
123        registered = sorted(self._policies) + sorted(self._sets)
124        raise CompositionError(
125            f"Unknown policy or policy_set: {name!r}. "
126            f"Registered: {registered}"
127        )

class PolicyAnalyzer: 
486class PolicyAnalyzer:
487    """
488    Static analysis engine for a single T.A.R.L. policy.
489
490    All methods return AnalysisResult.  When z3-solver is not installed every
491    result has available=False and carries an installation hint.
492    """
493
494    def __init__(self, policy: TarlPolicy) -> None:
495        self.policy = policy
496
497    def _translate(self) -> tuple:
498        tr = _ConditionToZ3()
499        tr.infer_types(self.policy.rules)
500        formulas = _build_formulas(tr, self.policy.rules)
501        return tr, formulas
502
503    # ── coverage ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
504
505    @_z3_serialized
506    def check_coverage(self) -> AnalysisResult:
507        """
508        Gap(P) = SAT(¬φ₁ ∧ ... ∧ ¬φₙ)
509
510        SAT  → coverage gap exists (DEFAULT-DENY reachable)
511        UNSAT → full coverage (every context matches a rule)
512        """
513        if not _Z3_AVAILABLE:
514            return _unavailable("coverage")
515        if not self.policy.rules:
516            return AnalysisResult(
517                kind="coverage", available=True, passed=False,
518                message="No rules — every context reaches DEFAULT-DENY",
519                gaps=[CoverageGap(description="Policy has no rules")],
520            )
521        tr, formulas = self._translate()
522        s = _z3.Solver()
523        s.add(*tr.domain_constraints())
524        s.add(*[_z3.Not(f) for f in formulas])
525        r = s.check()
526        if r == _z3.sat:
527            return AnalysisResult(
528                kind="coverage", available=True, passed=False,
529                message=f"Coverage gap found ({len(self.policy.rules)} rule(s) checked)",
530                gaps=[CoverageGap(
531                    description="Context region that falls through to DEFAULT-DENY",
532                    example_context=_model_dict(s.model(), tr),
533                )],
534            )
535        if r == _z3.unsat:
536            return AnalysisResult(
537                kind="coverage", available=True, passed=True,
538                message="Full coverage: every context matches at least one rule",
539            )
540        return AnalysisResult(
541            kind="coverage", available=True, passed=False,
542            message="Z3 returned unknown",
543        )
544
545    # ── shadows ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
546
547    @_z3_serialized
548    def check_shadows(self) -> AnalysisResult:
549        """
550        Reachable(rₖ) = SAT(¬φ₁ ∧ ... ∧ ¬φₖ₋₁ ∧ φₖ)
551
552        UNSAT → rule k is dead (shadowed by earlier rules).
553        """
554        if not _Z3_AVAILABLE:
555            return _unavailable("shadows")
556        if len(self.policy.rules) < 2:
557            return AnalysisResult(
558                kind="shadows", available=True, passed=True,
559                message="No shadowing possible with fewer than 2 rules",
560            )
561        tr, formulas = self._translate()
562        dead: list[ShadowedRule] = []
563        for k in range(1, len(formulas)):
564            s = _z3.Solver()
565            s.add(*tr.domain_constraints())
566            for i in range(k):
567                s.add(_z3.Not(formulas[i]))
568            s.add(formulas[k])
569            if s.check() == _z3.unsat:
570                rule = self.policy.rules[k]
571                dead.append(ShadowedRule(
572                    rule_index=k,
573                    condition=rule.condition,
574                    verdict=rule.verdict,
575                    shadowed_by=list(range(k)),
576                    description=(
577                        f"Rule [{k}] `when {rule.condition}` is unreachable; "
578                        f"rule(s) {list(range(k))} always match first"
579                    ),
580                ))
581        if dead:
582            return AnalysisResult(
583                kind="shadows", available=True, passed=False,
584                message=f"{len(dead)} dead rule(s) found",
585                shadows=dead,
586            )
587        return AnalysisResult(
588            kind="shadows", available=True, passed=True,
589            message="No dead rules detected",
590        )
591
592    # ── conflicts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
593
594    @_z3_serialized
595    def check_conflicts(self) -> AnalysisResult:
596        """
597        Conflict(rᵢ, rⱼ) = SAT(φᵢ ∧ φⱼ) where vᵢ ≠ vⱼ
598
599        SAT → both rules can fire for the same context (first-match-wins
600        resolves it, but it may be unintentional).
601        """
602        if not _Z3_AVAILABLE:
603            return _unavailable("conflicts")
604        tr, formulas = self._translate()
605        rules = self.policy.rules
606        found: list[ConflictPair] = []
607        for i in range(len(formulas)):
608            for j in range(i + 1, len(formulas)):
609                if rules[i].verdict == rules[j].verdict:
610                    continue
611                s = _z3.Solver()
612                s.add(*tr.domain_constraints())
613                s.add(formulas[i], formulas[j])
614                if s.check() == _z3.sat:
615                    found.append(ConflictPair(
616                        rule_i=i,
617                        rule_j=j,
618                        verdict_i=rules[i].verdict,
619                        verdict_j=rules[j].verdict,
620                        example_context=_model_dict(s.model(), tr),
621                        description=(
622                            f"Rules [{i}] ({rules[i].verdict.value}) and "
623                            f"[{j}] ({rules[j].verdict.value}) overlap. "
624                            f"First-match-wins resolves to rule [{i}]."
625                        ),
626                    ))
627        if found:
628            return AnalysisResult(
629                kind="conflicts", available=True, passed=False,
630                message=f"{len(found)} conflicting rule pair(s)",
631                conflicts=found,
632            )
633        return AnalysisResult(
634            kind="conflicts", available=True, passed=True,
635            message="No conflicts detected",
636        )
637
638    # ── equiv ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
639
640    @staticmethod
641    @_z3_serialized
642    def check_equiv(p1: TarlPolicy, p2: TarlPolicy) -> AnalysisResult:
643        """
644        SAT(V(P₁,c) ≠ V(P₂,c)) — not equivalent if satisfiable.
645        Uses a shared translator so both policies range over the same context.
646        """
647        if not _Z3_AVAILABLE:
648            return _unavailable("equiv")
649        tr = _ConditionToZ3()
650        tr.infer_types(p1.rules + p2.rules)
651        f1 = _build_formulas(tr, p1.rules)
652        f2 = _build_formulas(tr, p2.rules)
653        v1 = _verdict_ite(f1, p1.rules)
654        v2 = _verdict_ite(f2, p2.rules)
655        s = _z3.Solver()
656        s.add(*tr.domain_constraints())
657        s.add(v1 != v2)
658        r = s.check()
659        if r == _z3.unsat:
660            return AnalysisResult(
661                kind="equiv", available=True, passed=True,
662                message=f"'{p1.name}' and '{p2.name}' are equivalent",
663            )
664        if r == _z3.sat:
665            return AnalysisResult(
666                kind="equiv", available=True, passed=False,
667                message=f"'{p1.name}' and '{p2.name}' differ",
668                counterexample=_model_dict(s.model(), tr),
669            )
670        return AnalysisResult(
671            kind="equiv", available=True, passed=False,
672            message="Z3 returned unknown",
673        )
674
675    # ── refines ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
676
677    @staticmethod
678    @_z3_serialized
679    def check_refines(strict: TarlPolicy, permissive: TarlPolicy) -> AnalysisResult:
680        """
681        strict ⊑ permissive iff SAT(strict_allows ∧ ¬permissive_allows) is UNSAT.
682        I.e. strict never ALLOWs something that permissive would not ALLOW.
683        """
684        if not _Z3_AVAILABLE:
685            return _unavailable("refines")
686        tr = _ConditionToZ3()
687        tr.infer_types(strict.rules + permissive.rules)
688        fs = _build_formulas(tr, strict.rules)
689        fp = _build_formulas(tr, permissive.rules)
690        vs = _verdict_ite(fs, strict.rules)
691        vp = _verdict_ite(fp, permissive.rules)
692        _ALLOW = _z3.IntVal(_VERDICT_INT[TarlVerdict.ALLOW])
693        s = _z3.Solver()
694        s.add(*tr.domain_constraints())
695        s.add(vs == _ALLOW, vp != _ALLOW)
696        r = s.check()
697        if r == _z3.unsat:
698            return AnalysisResult(
699                kind="refines", available=True, passed=True,
700                message=(
701                    f"'{strict.name}' ⊑ '{permissive.name}': "
702                    "strict never allows what permissive would deny"
703                ),
704            )
705        if r == _z3.sat:
706            return AnalysisResult(
707                kind="refines", available=True, passed=False,
708                message=(
709                    f"'{strict.name}' is NOT a refinement of '{permissive.name}'"
710                ),
711                counterexample=_model_dict(s.model(), tr),
712            )
713        return AnalysisResult(
714            kind="refines", available=True, passed=False,
715            message="Z3 returned unknown",
716        )

All methods return AnalysisResult. When z3-solver is not installed every result has available=False and carries an installation hint.

@dataclass
class AnalysisResult: 
121@dataclass
122class AnalysisResult:
123    """Result of a static analysis query."""
124    kind: str
125    available: bool
126    passed: bool
127    message: str = ""
128    gaps: list[CoverageGap] = field(default_factory=list)
129    shadows: list[ShadowedRule] = field(default_factory=list)
130    conflicts: list[ConflictPair] = field(default_factory=list)
131    counterexample: dict[str, Any] | None = None
132
133    def __str__(self) -> str:
134        if not self.available:
135            return f"[{self.kind}] unavailable: {self.message}"
136        status = "PASS" if self.passed else "FAIL"
137        return f"[{self.kind}] {status}: {self.message}"
138
139    @property
140    def summary(self) -> str:
141        lines = [str(self)]
142        for g in self.gaps:
143            lines.append(f"  gap: {g.description}")
144            if g.example_context:
145                lines.append(f"    example: {g.example_context}")
146        for s in self.shadows:
147            lines.append(f"  dead: {s.description}")
148        for c in self.conflicts:
149            lines.append(f"  conflict: {c.description}")
150            if c.example_context:
151                lines.append(f"    example: {c.example_context}")
152        if self.counterexample:
153            lines.append(f"  counterexample: {self.counterexample}")
154        return "\n".join(lines)

140    def summary(self) -> str:
141        lines = [str(self)]
142        for g in self.gaps:
143            lines.append(f"  gap: {g.description}")
144            if g.example_context:
145                lines.append(f"    example: {g.example_context}")
146        for s in self.shadows:
147            lines.append(f"  dead: {s.description}")
148        for c in self.conflicts:
149            lines.append(f"  conflict: {c.description}")
150            if c.example_context:
151                lines.append(f"    example: {c.example_context}")
152        if self.counterexample:
153            lines.append(f"  counterexample: {self.counterexample}")
154        return "\n".join(lines)

class ProofVerifier: 
487class ProofVerifier:
488    """
489    Verifies TarlProof certificates independently of the runtime.
490
491    Usage::
492
493        verifier = ProofVerifier()
494        verifier.add_hmac_key("key1", b"my-secret")
495        verifier.add_ed25519_key("key2", ed25519_public_key)
496        result = verifier.verify(proof, policy_source=policy_text)
497        assert result.valid
498    """
499
500    def __init__(
501        self,
502        require_signature: bool = True,
503        allowed_signature_algorithms: set[str] | None = None,
504        require_policy_source: bool = False,
505        max_age_seconds: float | None = None,
506        revoked_policy_hashes: set[str] | None = None,
507        replay_guard: ReplayGuard | None = None,
508    ) -> None:
509        """
510        Verification options:
511
512          require_signature             — an unsigned proof is INVALID by
513                                          default; pass False only for explicit
514                                          local/permissive inspection.
515          allowed_signature_algorithms  — restrict accepted signature families
516                                          (e.g. {"ed25519"} rejects HMAC proofs).
517                                          Compared against the algorithm family
518                                          (``hmac`` / ``ed25519``).
519          require_policy_source         — verification without a policy_source to
520                                          bind policy_hash against is INVALID.
521          max_age_seconds               — reject proofs whose evaluated_at is
522                                          older than this (freshness; C024).
523          revoked_policy_hashes         — proofs bound to a revoked policy hash
524                                          are INVALID (policy revocation; C024).
525          replay_guard                  — a ReplayGuard; a proof already seen is
526                                          rejected as a replay (C023/C024).
527        """
528        self._hmac_keys: dict[str, bytes] = {}
529        self._ed25519_keys: dict[str, Ed25519PublicKey] = {}
530        self.require_signature = require_signature
531        self.allowed_signature_algorithms = (
532            {a.lower() for a in allowed_signature_algorithms}
533            if allowed_signature_algorithms is not None
534            else None
535        )
536        self.require_policy_source = require_policy_source
537        self.max_age_seconds = max_age_seconds
538        self.revoked_policy_hashes = revoked_policy_hashes or set()
539        self.replay_guard = replay_guard
540
541    def add_hmac_key(self, key_id: str, secret: bytes) -> ProofVerifier:
542        """Register an HMAC-SHA256 key for signature verification."""
543        self._hmac_keys[key_id] = secret
544        return self
545
546    def add_ed25519_key(
547        self, key_id: str, public_key: bytes | Ed25519PublicKey
548    ) -> ProofVerifier:
549        """Register an Ed25519 public key for signature verification."""
550        if isinstance(public_key, Ed25519PublicKey):
551            key = public_key
552        else:
553            key = Ed25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes(public_key)
554        self._ed25519_keys[key_id] = key
555        return self
556
557    def verify(
558        self,
559        proof: TarlProof,
560        policy_source: str | None = None,
561        expected_context: dict | None = None,
562        expected_evaluated_context: dict | None = None,
563        now: datetime.datetime | None = None,
564    ) -> VerificationResult:
565        """
566        Verify a TarlProof.
567
568        Checks performed:
569          signature    — HMAC-SHA256 or Ed25519 valid (or None if unsigned)
570          policy_hash  — matches provided policy_source (or None if not given)
571          trace        — internal consistency (k is first True in T)
572          context_coherence — positive proof binds an accepted representation
573                              and a supported transformation
574          context_schema_coherence — positive proof binds a passed schema
575                                     validation using that representation
576          context_binding   — original/evaluated hashes match expected_context
577          evaluated_context_binding — source-injected evaluated context matches
578                                      expected_evaluated_context
579          source_transformation — evaluated context differs only by valid,
580                                  top-level source namespace additions
581          expiry          — a time-bound proof matches the governing rule and
582                            remains live at an explicit trusted verification time
583
584        valid = True requires:
585          - signature is True, or None only when unsigned proofs were
586            explicitly allowed
587          - policy_hash is True or None (not provided)
588          - trace is True
589          - context_coherence is True
590          - context_schema_coherence is True
591        """
592        checks: dict[str, bool | None] = {}
593        messages: list[str] = []
594
595        structure_ok = _check_proof_structure(proof)
596        checks["structure"] = structure_ok
597        if not structure_ok:
598            return VerificationResult(
599                valid=False,
600                checks=checks,
601                message="proof structure INVALID",
602            )
603
604        # ── 1. Signature ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
605        sig_result = self._check_signature(proof)
606        if self.require_signature and sig_result is None:
607            # Strict mode: an unsigned proof is not acceptable.
608            sig_result = False
609        checks["signature"] = sig_result
610        if sig_result is True:
611            messages.append("signature valid")
612        elif sig_result is False:
613            messages.append(
614                "signature INVALID"
615                if proof.signature or not self.require_signature
616                else "signature REQUIRED but proof is unsigned"
617            )
618        else:
619            messages.append("signature skipped (unsigned)")
620
621        # ── 2. Policy hash ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
622        if policy_source is not None:
623            ph_ok = _check_policy_hash(proof, policy_source)
624            checks["policy_hash"] = ph_ok
625            messages.append(
626                "policy hash valid" if ph_ok else "policy hash MISMATCH"
627            )
628        elif self.require_policy_source:
629            # Strict mode: cannot certify policy binding without the source.
630            checks["policy_hash"] = False
631            messages.append("policy source REQUIRED but not provided")
632        else:
633            checks["policy_hash"] = None
634
635        # ── 3. Trace consistency ──────────────────────────────────────────────
636        trace_ok = _check_trace(proof)
637        checks["trace"] = trace_ok
638        messages.append(
639            "trace consistent" if trace_ok else "trace INCONSISTENT"
640        )
641
642        # ── 4. Context representation coherence ──────────────────────────────
643        coherence_ok = _check_context_coherence(proof)
644        checks["context_coherence"] = coherence_ok
645        messages.append(
646            "context representation coherent"
647            if coherence_ok
648            else "context representation INADMISSIBLE"
649        )
650
651        schema_coherence_ok = _check_context_schema_coherence(proof)
652        checks["context_schema_coherence"] = schema_coherence_ok
653        messages.append(
654            "context schema binding coherent"
655            if schema_coherence_ok
656            else "context schema binding INADMISSIBLE"
657        )
658
659        # ── 5. Context binding (C023: replay an old proof for a new context) ──
660        source_transformed = (
661            proof.normalization_algorithm_id
662            == "tarl.registered-source-injection"
663        )
664        prepared_expected_context = None
665        prepared_expected_evaluated_context = None
666        if expected_context is not None:
667            try:
668                prepared_expected_context = prepare_context(expected_context)
669            except ContextResolutionError:
670                cb_ok = False
671            else:
672                # The caller supplies the original request representation.  An
673                # identity evaluation must bind that same snapshot as canonical;
674                # a declared source-injection step may have a different evaluated
675                # hash, but must still bind the exact original request hash.
676                cb_ok = (
677                    proof.original_context_hash
678                    == prepared_expected_context.original_context_hash
679                )
680                if proof.normalization_algorithm_id == "identity":
681                    cb_ok = cb_ok and (
682                        proof.canonical_context_hash
683                        == prepared_expected_context.canonical_context_hash
684                        == proof.context_hash
685                    )
686            checks["context_binding"] = cb_ok
687            messages.append(
688                "context binds" if cb_ok else "context hash MISMATCH"
689            )
690        else:
691            checks["context_binding"] = False if source_transformed else None
692            if source_transformed:
693                messages.append(
694                    "original context REQUIRED for source-injected proof"
695                )
696
697        if expected_evaluated_context is not None:
698            try:
699                prepared_expected_evaluated_context = prepare_context(
700                    expected_evaluated_context,
701                    allow_source_keys=True,
702                )
703            except ContextResolutionError:
704                evaluated_cb_ok = False
705            else:
706                evaluated_cb_ok = (
707                    proof.canonical_context_hash
708                    == prepared_expected_evaluated_context.canonical_context_hash
709                    == proof.context_hash
710                )
711            checks["evaluated_context_binding"] = evaluated_cb_ok
712            messages.append(
713                "evaluated context binds"
714                if evaluated_cb_ok
715                else "evaluated context hash MISMATCH"
716            )
717        else:
718            checks["evaluated_context_binding"] = (
719                False if source_transformed else None
720            )
721            if source_transformed:
722                messages.append(
723                    "evaluated context REQUIRED for source-injected proof"
724                )
725
726        if source_transformed:
727            source_relation_ok = (
728                prepared_expected_context is not None
729                and prepared_expected_evaluated_context is not None
730                and _check_source_injection_relation(
731                    prepared_expected_context.canonical,
732                    prepared_expected_evaluated_context.canonical,
733                )
734            )
735            checks["source_transformation"] = source_relation_ok
736            messages.append(
737                "source transformation valid"
738                if source_relation_ok
739                else "source transformation INVALID"
740            )
741        else:
742            checks["source_transformation"] = None
743
744        expiry_ok, expiry_message = _check_policy_expiry(
745            proof,
746            policy_source,
747            now,
748        )
749        checks["expiry"] = expiry_ok
750        if expiry_message:
751            messages.append(expiry_message)
752
753        # Freshness (C024: replay a stale ALLOW)
754        if self.max_age_seconds is not None:
755            fr_ok = _check_freshness(proof, self.max_age_seconds, now)
756            checks["freshness"] = fr_ok
757            messages.append("fresh" if fr_ok else "proof is STALE")
758        else:
759            checks["freshness"] = None
760
761        # ── 7. Policy revocation (C024) ───────────────────────────────────────
762        if self.revoked_policy_hashes:
763            nr_ok = proof.policy_hash not in self.revoked_policy_hashes
764            checks["not_revoked"] = nr_ok
765            messages.append("policy current" if nr_ok else "policy REVOKED")
766        else:
767            checks["not_revoked"] = None
768
769        # ── 8. Replay (exact reuse of a previously-accepted proof) ────────────
770        non_replay_valid = (
771            sig_result is not False
772            and checks["policy_hash"] is not False
773            and trace_ok
774            and coherence_ok
775            and schema_coherence_ok
776            and checks["context_binding"] is not False
777            and checks["evaluated_context_binding"] is not False
778            and checks["source_transformation"] is not False
779            and checks["expiry"] is not False
780            and checks["freshness"] is not False
781            and checks["not_revoked"] is not False
782        )
783
784        if self.replay_guard is None:
785            checks["not_replayed"] = None
786        elif not non_replay_valid:
787            checks["not_replayed"] = None
788            messages.append("replay recording skipped for invalid proof")
789        else:
790            fresh = self.replay_guard.check_and_record(proof)
791            checks["not_replayed"] = fresh
792            messages.append("first use" if fresh else "REPLAYED proof")
793
794        valid = (
795            non_replay_valid
796            and checks["not_replayed"] is not False
797        )
798
799        return VerificationResult(
800            valid=valid,
801            checks=checks,
802            message="; ".join(messages),
803        )
804
805    def _check_signature(self, proof: TarlProof) -> bool | None:
806        """
807        Returns True if the signature is cryptographically valid.
808        Returns False if invalid or the key is unknown.
809        Returns None if the proof has no signature.
810        """
811        if not proof.signature:
812            return None
813
814        alg, sep, sig_hex = proof.signature.partition(":")
815        if not sep:
816            return False
817
818        # Strict mode: reject signature families outside the allow-list (e.g.
819        # an HMAC proof presented to an Ed25519-only verifier).
820        if self.allowed_signature_algorithms is not None:
821            family = alg.split("-", 1)[0].lower()
822            if family not in self.allowed_signature_algorithms:
823                return False
824
825        if alg == "hmac-sha256":
826            secret = self._hmac_keys.get(proof.key_id)
827            if secret is None:
828                return False
829            supplied = _decode_canonical_hex(sig_hex, hashlib.sha256().digest_size)
830            if supplied is None:
831                return False
832            expected = hmac.new(
833                secret, proof.canonical_bytes(), hashlib.sha256
834            ).digest()
835            return hmac.compare_digest(expected, supplied)
836
837        if alg == "ed25519":
838            public_key = self._ed25519_keys.get(proof.key_id)
839            if public_key is None:
840                return False
841            supplied = _decode_canonical_hex(sig_hex, 64)
842            if supplied is None:
843                return False
844            try:
845                public_key.verify(
846                    supplied, proof.canonical_bytes()
847                )
848                return True
849            except (ValueError, InvalidSignature):
850                return False
851
852        return False  # unknown algorithm

verifier.add_ed25519_key("key2", ed25519_public_key)

assert result.valid

680                if proof.normalization_algorithm_id == "identity":
681                    cb_ok = cb_ok and (
682                        proof.canonical_context_hash
683                        == prepared_expected_context.canonical_context_hash
684                        == proof.context_hash
685                    )
686            checks["context_binding"] = cb_ok
687            messages.append(
688                "context binds" if cb_ok else "context hash MISMATCH"
689            )
690        else:
691            checks["context_binding"] = False if source_transformed else None
692            if source_transformed:
693                messages.append(
694                    "original context REQUIRED for source-injected proof"
695                )
696
697        if expected_evaluated_context is not None:
698            try:
699                prepared_expected_evaluated_context = prepare_context(
700                    expected_evaluated_context,
701                    allow_source_keys=True,
702                )
703            except ContextResolutionError:
704                evaluated_cb_ok = False
705            else:
706                evaluated_cb_ok = (
707                    proof.canonical_context_hash
708                    == prepared_expected_evaluated_context.canonical_context_hash
709                    == proof.context_hash
710                )
711            checks["evaluated_context_binding"] = evaluated_cb_ok
712            messages.append(
713                "evaluated context binds"
714                if evaluated_cb_ok
715                else "evaluated context hash MISMATCH"
716            )
717        else:
718            checks["evaluated_context_binding"] = (
719                False if source_transformed else None
720            )
721            if source_transformed:
722                messages.append(
723                    "evaluated context REQUIRED for source-injected proof"
724                )
725
726        if source_transformed:
727            source_relation_ok = (
728                prepared_expected_context is not None
729                and prepared_expected_evaluated_context is not None
730                and _check_source_injection_relation(
731                    prepared_expected_context.canonical,
732                    prepared_expected_evaluated_context.canonical,
733                )
734            )
735            checks["source_transformation"] = source_relation_ok
736            messages.append(
737                "source transformation valid"
738                if source_relation_ok
739                else "source transformation INVALID"
740            )
741        else:
742            checks["source_transformation"] = None
743
744        expiry_ok, expiry_message = _check_policy_expiry(
745            proof,
746            policy_source,
747            now,
748        )
749        checks["expiry"] = expiry_ok
750        if expiry_message:
751            messages.append(expiry_message)
752
753        # Freshness (C024: replay a stale ALLOW)
754        if self.max_age_seconds is not None:
755            fr_ok = _check_freshness(proof, self.max_age_seconds, now)
756            checks["freshness"] = fr_ok
757            messages.append("fresh" if fr_ok else "proof is STALE")
758        else:
759            checks["freshness"] = None
760
761        # ── 7. Policy revocation (C024) ───────────────────────────────────────
762        if self.revoked_policy_hashes:
763            nr_ok = proof.policy_hash not in self.revoked_policy_hashes
764            checks["not_revoked"] = nr_ok
765            messages.append("policy current" if nr_ok else "policy REVOKED")
766        else:
767            checks["not_revoked"] = None
768
769        # ── 8. Replay (exact reuse of a previously-accepted proof) ────────────
770        non_replay_valid = (
771            sig_result is not False
772            and checks["policy_hash"] is not False
773            and trace_ok
774            and coherence_ok
775            and schema_coherence_ok
776            and checks["context_binding"] is not False
777            and checks["evaluated_context_binding"] is not False
778            and checks["source_transformation"] is not False
779            and checks["expiry"] is not False
780            and checks["freshness"] is not False
781            and checks["not_revoked"] is not False
782        )
783
784        if self.replay_guard is None:
785            checks["not_replayed"] = None
786        elif not non_replay_valid:
787            checks["not_replayed"] = None
788            messages.append("replay recording skipped for invalid proof")
789        else:
790            fresh = self.replay_guard.check_and_record(proof)
791            checks["not_replayed"] = fresh
792            messages.append("first use" if fresh else "REPLAYED proof")
793
794        valid = (
795            non_replay_valid
796            and checks["not_replayed"] is not False
797        )
798
799        return VerificationResult(
800            valid=valid,
801            checks=checks,
802            message="; ".join(messages),
803        )

Verify a TarlProof.

Checks performed: signature — HMAC-SHA256 or Ed25519 valid (or None if unsigned) policy_hash — matches provided policy_source (or None if not given) trace — internal consistency (k is first True in T) context_coherence — positive proof binds an accepted representation and a supported transformation context_schema_coherence — positive proof binds a passed schema validation using that representation context_binding — original/evaluated hashes match expected_context evaluated_context_binding — source-injected evaluated context matches expected_evaluated_context source_transformation — evaluated context differs only by valid, top-level source namespace additions expiry — a time-bound proof matches the governing rule and remains live at an explicit trusted verification time

valid = True requires:

  • signature is True, or None only when unsigned proofs were explicitly allowed
  • policy_hash is True or None (not provided)
  • trace is True
  • context_coherence is True
  • context_schema_coherence is True

def context_authority_admissible( proof: TarlProof, expected_verdict: TarlVerdict) -> bool: 
209def context_authority_admissible(
210    proof: TarlProof,
211    expected_verdict: TarlVerdict,
212) -> bool:
213    """Return whether a proof can participate in an authority transition.
214
215    This requires a structurally coherent matched-rule proof plus context and
216    schema coherence. Consumers that accept proofs across a trust boundary must
217    still use :class:`ProofVerifier` for signatures, policy binding, freshness,
218    replay, temporal authority, and expected contexts.
219    """
220    return (
221        _check_proof_structure(proof)
222        and proof.verdict is expected_verdict
223        and proof.rule_index >= 0
224        and _check_trace(proof)
225        and _check_context_coherence(proof)
226        and _check_context_schema_coherence(proof)
227        and proof.context_schema_validation_status == "passed"
228    )

class TarlAuditArchive: 
 52class TarlAuditArchive:
 53    """
 54    Append-only audit log of TarlProof certificates backed by SQLite.
 55
 56    Thread-safe: concurrent stores and queries are serialised by an
 57    internal lock.  Use the context-manager form to ensure the connection
 58    is closed properly::
 59
 60        with TarlAuditArchive("tarl_audit.db") as archive:
 61            archive.store(proof)
 62
 63    Or manage the lifecycle manually with :meth:`close`.
 64    """
 65
 66    def __init__(self, db_path: str = "tarl_audit.db") -> None:
 67        self._path = db_path
 68        self._conn: sqlite3.Connection | None = None
 69        self._lock = threading.Lock()
 70        self._ensure_schema()
 71
 72    # ── Schema ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 73
 74    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
 75        if self._conn is None:
 76            self._conn = sqlite3.connect(
 77                self._path, check_same_thread=False
 78            )
 79        return self._conn
 80
 81    def _ensure_schema(self) -> None:
 82        with self._lock:
 83            conn = self._connect()
 84            conn.executescript("""
 85                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS proofs (
 86                    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
 87                    policy_hash   TEXT    NOT NULL,
 88                    context_hash  TEXT    NOT NULL,
 89                    verdict       TEXT    NOT NULL,
 90                    rule_index    INTEGER NOT NULL,
 91                    evaluated_at  TEXT    NOT NULL,
 92                    expires_at    TEXT,
 93                    signature     TEXT,
 94                    proof_json    TEXT    NOT NULL,
 95                    prev_hash     TEXT,
 96                    entry_hash    TEXT
 97                );
 98                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_verdict
 99                    ON proofs (verdict);
100                CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_evaluated_at
101                    ON proofs (evaluated_at);
102            """)
103            # Migrate older archives that predate the hash chain.
104            existing = {r[1] for r in conn.execute(
105                "PRAGMA table_info(proofs)").fetchall()}
106            for col in ("prev_hash", "entry_hash"):
107                if col not in existing:
108                    conn.execute(f"ALTER TABLE proofs ADD COLUMN {col} TEXT")
109            conn.commit()
110
111    # ── Write ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
112
113    def store(
114        self,
115        proof: TarlProof,
116        expires_at: str | None = None,
117    ) -> int:
118        """
119        Persist a proof in the archive.
120
121        :param proof:       The TarlProof to store.
122        :param expires_at:  Optional ISO-8601 UTC expiry from TarlDecision.expires_at.
123        :returns:           Row id of the inserted record.
124        """
125        proof_json = proof.to_json()
126        with self._lock:
127            conn = self._connect()
128            # Link this record to the current chain head (genesis if empty).
129            head = conn.execute(
130                "SELECT entry_hash FROM proofs ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1"
131            ).fetchone()
132            prev_hash = head[0] if head and head[0] else _GENESIS
133            entry_hash = _entry_hash(prev_hash, proof_json)
134            cursor = conn.execute(
135                """INSERT INTO proofs
136                   (policy_hash, context_hash, verdict, rule_index,
137                    evaluated_at, expires_at, signature, proof_json,
138                    prev_hash, entry_hash)
139                   VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
140                (
141                    proof.policy_hash,
142                    proof.context_hash,
143                    proof.verdict.value,
144                    proof.rule_index,
145                    proof.evaluated_at,
146                    expires_at,
147                    proof.signature or None,
148                    proof_json,
149                    prev_hash,
150                    entry_hash,
151                ),
152            )
153            conn.commit()
154            # lastrowid is the new AUTOINCREMENT id after a successful INSERT;
155            # it is only None if no row was inserted (never on this path).
156            return cursor.lastrowid or 0
157
158    # ── Read ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
159
160    def query(
161        self,
162        verdict: str | None = None,
163        from_dt: str | None = None,
164        to_dt: str | None = None,
165        limit: int = 100,
166        verifier=None,
167    ) -> list[TarlProof]:
168        """
169        Query stored proofs, newest first.
170
171        :param verdict:   Filter by verdict ("ALLOW", "DENY", or "ESCALATE").
172        :param from_dt:   ISO-8601 lower bound on evaluated_at (inclusive).
173        :param to_dt:     ISO-8601 upper bound on evaluated_at (inclusive).
174        :param limit:     Maximum number of results (default 100).
175        :param verifier:  Optional ProofVerifier.  When supplied, proofs whose
176                          signature check returns False (cryptographically
177                          invalid) are excluded from results.  Unsigned proofs
178                          (signature="") are kept; only actively invalid
179                          signatures are rejected.  Without a verifier, rows
180                          are returned as-is from SQLite with no tamper check
181                          — callers that need tamper-evidence must pass one.
182        :returns:         List of TarlProof objects.
183        """
184        conditions: list[str] = []
185        params: list = []
186        if verdict:
187            conditions.append("verdict = ?")
188            params.append(verdict.upper())
189        if from_dt:
190            conditions.append("evaluated_at >= ?")
191            params.append(from_dt)
192        if to_dt:
193            conditions.append("evaluated_at <= ?")
194            params.append(to_dt)
195        where = ("WHERE " + " AND ".join(conditions)) if conditions else ""
196        params.append(limit)
197        with self._lock:
198            conn = self._connect()
199            rows = conn.execute(
200                f"SELECT proof_json FROM proofs {where} "
201                f"ORDER BY evaluated_at DESC LIMIT ?",
202                params,
203            ).fetchall()
204        proofs = [TarlProof.from_json(row[0]) for row in rows]
205        if verifier is not None:
206            proofs = [
207                p for p in proofs
208                if verifier.verify(p).checks.get("signature") is not False
209            ]
210        return proofs
211
212    def count(
213        self,
214        verdict: str | None = None,
215        from_dt: str | None = None,
216        to_dt: str | None = None,
217    ) -> int:
218        """Count proofs matching the given filters."""
219        conditions: list[str] = []
220        params: list = []
221        if verdict:
222            conditions.append("verdict = ?")
223            params.append(verdict.upper())
224        if from_dt:
225            conditions.append("evaluated_at >= ?")
226            params.append(from_dt)
227        if to_dt:
228            conditions.append("evaluated_at <= ?")
229            params.append(to_dt)
230        where = ("WHERE " + " AND ".join(conditions)) if conditions else ""
231        with self._lock:
232            conn = self._connect()
233            row = conn.execute(
234                f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM proofs {where}", params
235            ).fetchone()
236        return int(row[0]) if row else 0
237
238    # ── Tamper-evidence ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
239
240    def head_hash(self) -> str:
241        """Return the current chain head (latest entry_hash), or genesis if empty.
242
243        Persist this externally as a checkpoint: a later ``verify_chain`` whose
244        head differs from a trusted checkpoint reveals suffix rewriting even if
245        the chain re-links internally."""
246        with self._lock:
247            conn = self._connect()
248            row = conn.execute(
249                "SELECT entry_hash FROM proofs ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1"
250            ).fetchone()
251        return str(row[0]) if row and row[0] else _GENESIS
252
253    def verify_chain(
254        self, expected_head: str | None = None
255    ) -> ChainVerification:
256        """Walk the hash chain in insertion order and report its integrity.
257
258        Detects record tampering (a modified ``proof_json`` no longer hashes to
259        its stored ``entry_hash``), deletion/reordering (a record's ``prev_hash``
260        no longer matches its predecessor's ``entry_hash``), and a tampered head.
261
262        ``expected_head`` is a trusted external checkpoint (see :meth:`head_hash`
263        and ``tarl audit checkpoint``). A chain that re-links internally but
264        whose head differs from the checkpoint reveals suffix rewriting or
265        truncation — the case the internal walk alone cannot catch.
266        """
267        with self._lock:
268            conn = self._connect()
269            rows = conn.execute(
270                "SELECT id, proof_json, prev_hash, entry_hash "
271                "FROM proofs ORDER BY id ASC"
272            ).fetchall()
273        prev = _GENESIS
274        for row_id, proof_json, prev_hash, entry_hash in rows:
275            if prev_hash != prev:
276                return ChainVerification(
277                    False, len(rows), row_id,
278                    "prev_hash does not match the preceding record "
279                    "(deletion, insertion, or reordering)")
280            expected = _entry_hash(prev, proof_json)
281            if entry_hash != expected:
282                return ChainVerification(
283                    False, len(rows), row_id,
284                    "record contents do not match entry_hash (tampered)")
285            prev = entry_hash
286        if expected_head is not None and prev != expected_head:
287            return ChainVerification(
288                False, len(rows), None,
289                f"chain head {prev!r} does not match the trusted checkpoint "
290                f"{expected_head!r} (suffix rewrite or truncation)")
291        return ChainVerification(True, len(rows))
292
293    # ── Lifecycle ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
294
295    def close(self) -> None:
296        """Close the database connection."""
297        with self._lock:
298            if self._conn is not None:
299                self._conn.close()
300                self._conn = None
301
302    def __enter__(self) -> TarlAuditArchive:
303        return self
304
305    def __exit__(self, *_) -> None:
306        self.close()

Append-only audit log of TarlProof certificates backed by SQLite.

Thread-safe: concurrent stores and queries are serialised by an internal lock. Use the context-manager form to ensure the connection is closed properly::

with TarlAuditArchive("tarl_audit.db") as archive:
    archive.store(proof)

Or manage the lifecycle manually with close().

268            conn = self._connect()
269            rows = conn.execute(
270                "SELECT id, proof_json, prev_hash, entry_hash "
271                "FROM proofs ORDER BY id ASC"
272            ).fetchall()
273        prev = _GENESIS
274        for row_id, proof_json, prev_hash, entry_hash in rows:
275            if prev_hash != prev:
276                return ChainVerification(
277                    False, len(rows), row_id,
278                    "prev_hash does not match the preceding record "
279                    "(deletion, insertion, or reordering)")
280            expected = _entry_hash(prev, proof_json)
281            if entry_hash != expected:
282                return ChainVerification(
283                    False, len(rows), row_id,
284                    "record contents do not match entry_hash (tampered)")
285            prev = entry_hash
286        if expected_head is not None and prev != expected_head:
287            return ChainVerification(
288                False, len(rows), None,
289                f"chain head {prev!r} does not match the trusted checkpoint "
290                f"{expected_head!r} (suffix rewrite or truncation)")
291        return ChainVerification(True, len(rows))

Walk the hash chain in insertion order and report its integrity.

Detects record tampering (a modified proof_json no longer hashes to its stored entry_hash), deletion/reordering (a record's prev_hash no longer matches its predecessor's entry_hash), and a tampered head.

expected_head is a trusted external checkpoint (see head_hash() and tarl audit checkpoint). A chain that re-links internally but whose head differs from the checkpoint reveals suffix rewriting or truncation — the case the internal walk alone cannot catch.

def close(self) -> None: 
295    def close(self) -> None:
296        """Close the database connection."""
297        with self._lock:
298            if self._conn is not None:
299                self._conn.close()
300                self._conn = None

class TarlExplainer: 
 96class TarlExplainer:
 97    """
 98    Explains T.A.R.L. policy evaluations in human-readable form.
 99
100    Evaluates a policy rule-by-rule, recording why each rule matched or
101    did not, and returns a :class:`PolicyExplanation` with the full trace.
102
103    Usage::
104
105        explainer = TarlExplainer()
106        exp = explainer.explain({"user": {"role": "admin"}}, policy_text=src)
107        print(exp.format())
108    """
109
110    def explain(
111        self,
112        context: dict,
113        policy_text: str = "",
114        policy: TarlPolicy | None = None,
115    ) -> PolicyExplanation:
116        """
117        Evaluate a policy against context and return a full explanation.
118
119        :param context:     The evaluation context dict.
120        :param policy_text: Policy source text (used if policy is None).
121        :param policy:      Pre-parsed TarlPolicy (takes precedence).
122        """
123        from utf.tarl.core import PolicyParser, SafeExpr, _check_policy_temporal
124
125        if policy is None:
126            if not policy_text:
127                return PolicyExplanation(
128                    policy_name="unnamed",
129                    verdict=TarlVerdict.DENY,
130                    matched_rule_index=-1,
131                )
132            policy = PolicyParser.parse(policy_text)
133
134        # Temporal window check fires before any rule evaluation
135        temporal = _check_policy_temporal(policy)
136        if temporal is not None:
137            return PolicyExplanation(
138                policy_name=policy.name,
139                verdict=temporal.verdict,
140                matched_rule_index=-1,
141                temporal_reason=temporal.reason,
142            )
143
144        traces: list[RuleTrace] = []
145        matched_index = -1
146        expires_at = None
147
148        for i, rule in enumerate(policy.rules):
149            if matched_index >= 0:
150                traces.append(RuleTrace(
151                    rule_index=i,
152                    condition=rule.condition,
153                    verdict=rule.verdict,
154                    matched=False,
155                    evaluated=False,
156                ))
157                continue
158
159            error = None
160            matched = False
161            try:
162                matched = bool(SafeExpr.evaluate(rule.condition, context))
163            except Exception as exc:
164                error = str(exc)
165
166            traces.append(RuleTrace(
167                rule_index=i,
168                condition=rule.condition,
169                verdict=rule.verdict,
170                matched=matched,
171                evaluated=True,
172                error=error,
173            ))
174
175            # An unresolved or ill-typed value is not an ordinary non-match.
176            # Stop the trace at the failing rule so a later permissive rule is
177            # never presented as the decision path.
178            if error is not None:
179                break
180
181            if matched:
182                matched_index = i
183                if rule.duration_seconds:
184                    expires_at = (
185                        datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
186                        + datetime.timedelta(seconds=rule.duration_seconds)
187                    ).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
188
189        verdict = (
190            policy.rules[matched_index].verdict
191            if matched_index >= 0
192            else TarlVerdict.DENY
193        )
194
195        return PolicyExplanation(
196            policy_name=policy.name,
197            verdict=verdict,
198            matched_rule_index=matched_index,
199            rule_traces=traces,
200            expires_at=expires_at,
201        )

Usage::

explainer = TarlExplainer()

print(exp.format())

38@dataclass
39class PolicyExplanation:
40    """Full explanation of a policy evaluation."""
41    policy_name: str
42    verdict: TarlVerdict
43    matched_rule_index: int               # -1 = DEFAULT_DENY
44    rule_traces: list[RuleTrace] = field(default_factory=list)
45    temporal_reason: str | None = None
46    expires_at: str | None = None
47
48    def format(self, verbose: bool = False) -> str:
49        """
50        Return a human-readable explanation string.
51
52        :param verbose: When True, include skipped rules in the trace.
53        """
54        lines = [
55            f"Policy:   {self.policy_name}",
56            f"Verdict:  {self.verdict.value}",
57        ]
58        if self.matched_rule_index >= 0:
59            lines.append(f"Matched:  Rule #{self.matched_rule_index}")
60        else:
61            lines.append("Matched:  DEFAULT_DENY (no rule matched)")
62        if self.expires_at:
63            lines.append(f"Expires:  {self.expires_at}")
64        if self.temporal_reason:
65            lines.append(f"\nTemporal: {self.temporal_reason}")
66            return "\n".join(lines)
67        if not self.rule_traces:
68            return "\n".join(lines)
69        lines.append("\nRule evaluation trace:")
70        for trace in self.rule_traces:
71            if verbose or trace.evaluated:
72                lines.append(str(trace))
73        return "\n".join(lines)
74
75    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
76        return {
77            "policy_name": self.policy_name,
78            "verdict": self.verdict.value,
79            "matched_rule_index": self.matched_rule_index,
80            "expires_at": self.expires_at,
81            "temporal_reason": self.temporal_reason,
82            "rule_traces": [
83                {
84                    "rule_index": t.rule_index,
85                    "condition": t.condition,
86                    "verdict": t.verdict.value,
87                    "matched": t.matched,
88                    "evaluated": t.evaluated,
89                    "error": t.error,
90                }
91                for t in self.rule_traces
92            ],
93        }

class RuleTrace: 
16@dataclass
17class RuleTrace:
18    """Evaluation trace for a single rule."""
19    rule_index: int
20    condition: str
21    verdict: TarlVerdict
22    matched: bool
23    evaluated: bool = True       # False if skipped — earlier rule already matched
24    error: str | None = None
25
26    def __str__(self) -> str:
27        if not self.evaluated:
28            return f"  [{self.rule_index}] (skipped — earlier rule matched)"
29        status = "MATCHED" if self.matched else "no match"
30        err = f"  [error: {self.error}]" if self.error else ""
31        return (
32            f"  [{self.rule_index}] when {self.condition}"
33            f" => {self.verdict.value}"
34            f"  →  {status}{err}"
35        )
